eng: She is trying on red boots.

kam: Mai kuaniiya!
eng: They don't fit!

kam: Tene tene vyũ, kũyaĩ kĩvindu ndũanĩ ya Opio. Andũ makomaa manoa na methũkũma masalũkĩtye.
eng: Long ago, there was no night in Opio's village. People slept when they were tired and worked when they were awake.

kam: Mũthenya ũmwe Opio aĩna ũtanu mwingĩ nũndũ nĩw'o waĩ mũthenya wake wa mbee kũthi kũsyĩma eweka. Opio nĩwosie makitĩ na aumala ndũanĩ. Kavinda kanini kathela makitĩ nĩmanzĩe kũsembany'a nzaaĩ. Opio nĩwamatĩĩe na asemba kĩlungu kya masaa maingĩ. Anoa nĩwathũmũaa na ĩndĩ esemba ĩngĩ. Ndaona makitĩ make.
eng: One day Opio went out hunting with his dogs. After a short time, his dogs started to chase an antelope. Opio followed them. He ran for many hours. Every time he became tired, he rested. Then he would run again. But he could not find his dogs.

kam: Ĩtina wa matukũ maingĩ nĩwavikie ndũanĩ yaĩna andũ anini mailye mbee wa nyũmba syoo. Nĩwendie nyũmbanĩ ĩmwe na eea mwene, "nĩsembanĩtye na Nzaaĩ ĩvinda ĩasa mũno na nenda kũthũmũa."Mwene nyũmba nĩwaisye, "ĩkala nthĩ ũthũmũe. Nũkwenda ũkĩ?" Opio nĩwew'aa waũni mũno kwou nĩwanyuie ũkĩ na akoma.
eng: After many days, he came to a village. He went to one of the houses and said to the owner, "I have chased an antelope for a long time and I am very tired. I want to rest." The man said, "Sit down and rest. Would you like some beer?" Opio was very thirsty so he drank some. Then he went to sleep.

kam: Akũkĩla ndonaa nthĩ. Nĩwavingũie na kũvĩnga metho make mavinda maingĩ na anzĩĩa kwona ũla mũndũ ailye mbee wa nyũmba. Nĩweie mũndũ ũsu, "ũnengie kĩndũ kĩthũku mũno; ndĩkwona nesa."
eng: When he woke up, he couldn't see. He opened and closed his eyes many times. "You have given me something very bad to drink," he said to the man. "I can't see properly anymore!" "There is nothing wrong with you," the man replied. "It's night now. Haven't you ever seen night? When the day leaves, the night comes."

kam: Mwene nyũmba nĩwamũie, "vaĩ kĩndũ kĩthũku naku. Oyu nĩ ũtukũ. Nũndũ ũtoona ũtukũ. Mũthenya wathi, ũtukũ nĩũkaa. Twĩthĩwaa na masaa ĩkũmi na elĩ ma ũtukũ. Tũthũmũa ũtukũ na twĩthũkũma mũthenya. Wĩkalaa va? Ndũanĩ yenyu ndĩ ũtukũ ĩĩ?" Opio nĩwakũlilye makũlyo maingĩ ĩũlũ wa ũtukũ nũndũ nĩwendie ũtukũ mũno. Ndaakoma ĩngĩ; manenie na mwene nyũmba mbaka kwakya. Opio nĩwendie kwĩkala mũthenya ũngĩ nĩkana one ũtukũ ũkũka ĩngĩ.
eng: Opio asked many questions about the night. He began to like it very much. He and his new friend talked until morning. He stayed for another day so that he could see the night come again.

kam: Nĩwakomie mũthenya na okĩla ũtukũ ũtanavika. Nĩwakũlilye mwene nyũmba amũtavye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩkana atwae ũtukũ ndũanĩ yake andũ make matonye kũwona. Opio nĩweiwe athi okone sivũ.
eng: The next morning he asked his friend, "How can I take the night to my own village? I want my people to see the night." "When it starts to get dark this evening, walk to your village. If you look straight in front, the night will follow you. But you must not look back. If you look back, the night will go away."

kam: Sivũ nĩweie Opio atembee athi ndũanĩ yake wioo ũla waatĩe. Ndaĩlĩte kũsisya ĩtina nĩkana ũtukũ ndũkasyoke. Opio nĩwekie ũndũ wataviwe na anzĩĩa kũtembea aendete ndũanĩ yake. Nĩwendaa kũsisya ĩtina ĩndĩ ndatata kwĩka ou. Nĩwendie mbaka anzĩĩa kwona ndũa na anyanyae make.
eng: Opio did as he was told. That evening, he began to walk towards his village. He felt the dark night behind him as he walked. He wanted to look back. But he did not.

kam: Mona Opio andũ ma ndũa nĩmakĩie. Nĩmanzĩĩe kũlonza makwasya, "ni kyaũ watwetee, Opio? Kĩndũ kĩĩ kĩkwatĩĩe nĩkyũtũaa. Kĩĩ nĩ kĩvindu kya kyaũ kĩkwatĩe?" Opio nĩwaisye, "anyanyawa, kĩvindu kĩĩ nĩ ũtukũ. Mwĩna vw'ĩa; onakwa naĩna vw'ĩa."
eng: When he came to his village, the villagers were afraid. "What disease have you brought to us, Opio?" they asked. "What is this dark thing following you?" Opio said, "My friends, this dark thing is called night. Now you are afraid and I was afraid, too."

kam: Na ou nĩw'o ũtukũ wokie ndũanĩ ya Opio.
eng: And that is how night came to Opio's village.

kam: Langi wa keli ni wa isungwa.
eng: They reached a river and found a large buffalo drinking water.

kam: Thii ni isungwa.
eng: Hare wanted to know who was stronger, Buffalo or Elephant.

kam: Matu ni ma mbuluu.
eng: Buffalo and Elephant pulled. Elephant pulled Buffalo.

kam: Langi wa thanthatu ni wa mbuluu ngwatu.
eng: Buffalo pulled Elephant. Neither could win.

kam: Matunda aa ni ma langi wa mbuluu ngwatu.
eng: From where he was hiding, Hare continued to eat Elephant's honey.

kam: Langi wa mwonza ni wa nthambalau.
eng: After he had finished the honey, he cut the rope closer to Buffalo.

kam: Ngua yakwa ni ya langi wa nthambalau. Ni langi niwendete muno!
eng: Elephant fell over hard and hit a tree.

kam: Niwise langi syonthe sya utathi?
eng: Hare went to Buffalo and praised her, saying that she was stronger.

kam: King'angi ki mayo manene.
eng: A crocodile has big teeth.

kam: Munyambu wi mayo manene onaw'o.
eng: A lion has big teeth as well.

kam: Ng'ombe yi maeo mevinya.
eng: A cow has strong teeth.

kam: Masuni mai mayo.
eng: Birds do not have teeth.

kam: Mbiya syi mayo manene mambee.
eng: Rats have big front teeth.

kam: Makuyu me mayo moii.
eng: Sharks have sharp teeth.

kam: Nethiyawa na mayo maingi.
eng: I used to have a lot of teeth.

kam: Nayuyu ndina mayo maingi.
eng: But now I don't have many.

kam: Nau endete ũsũũ.
eng: Dad loves porridge.

kam: Nyie nendete konivulekisi.
eng: I love cornflakes.

kam: Nau endete Kaawa.
eng: Dad loves coffee.

kam: Nyie nendete ĩia.
eng: I love milk.

kam: Nau endete matunda ma mũthemba wa avoo.
eng: Dad loves apples.

kam: Nyie nendete masungwa.
eng: I love oranges.

kam: Nau endete mukate. ĩndi nyie nendete mũkate wa tositi.
eng: Dad loves bread. I love toasted bread.

kam: Ĩthyĩ twĩ eli nĩtwendete itumbũa.
eng: We both love fat cakes (vetkoek).

kam: Nonisome.
eng: Nomsa overhears Jabu and Zodwa talking and she's curious. She asks them what's wrong with cutting the loaf into five pieces for kotas. Zodwa and Jabu reply together, "A kota is a quarter of a loaf!" Nomsa still looks confused, so Zodwa explains, "The loaf must be cut into four equal pieces. Otherwise, they are not quarters."

kam: Nonie ĩloli ĩtwaĩtwe kĩtheonĩ kya lelũ.
eng: I saw a big truck driving down the road.

kam: Mũtokaa mũthemba wa Ma naw'o watwaĩtwe ũlĩsĩte lelũni.
eng: A car came driving up the road.

kam: Ndeleva wa ĩloli nĩwanenaa na simũ ya moko.
eng: The truck driver was talking on his cellphone.

kam: Ndasisasyaa lelũ.
eng: He was not looking at the road.

kam: Nĩkwethĩiw'e na mbanga nene.
eng: There was a big accident.

kam: Ambyulenzi na volisi nĩmavikie kunengane utethyo.
eng: An ambulance and the police came to help.

kam: Maloli elĩ ma kũkusya ngalĩ nomokie. Ĩmwe nĩyakusisye ĩloli na ĩngĩ yakusya kaa.
eng: Two tow trucks came. They towed the truck and the car.

kam: Nĩnatelemile.
eng: I was shocked.

kam: Tene tene vyu vaĩ na mũndũũme wekalaa na mũka na kũmwenda mũno. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩwaendie kĩthekanĩ. Enzĩanĩ nĩwakomanie na mwĩĩtu mũasa, mũtheke na mwanake. Nĩwamwendie kwa mĩtukĩ. Mwĩĩtu nake nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlile omĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ amũtavya kana enondo ĩmwe tu.
eng: A long time ago, there was a man who lived with his wife whom he loved very much. One day he took a walk to the forest. Along the way, he met a tall, slender, and very beautiful girl. He fell in love with her at first sight. The girl too readily accepted him. But she told him that she had only one breast.

kam: Nĩwamũie athi mũsyĩ akatile mũka nondo ĩmwe amwetee avikye nondo ilĩ nikana matonye kũtwaana. Mũndũũme ũsu nĩwasembie mũsyĩ, osa kavyũ, avalũkya mũka nthĩ, na omĩtũkĩ amũtila nondo.
eng: So she told him to go home, cut off one of his wife's breasts and bring it to her. Then she would have two breasts, and they could marry. The man ran very fast back home, picked a knife, pounced on his dear wife, and the breast was off instantly.

kam: Nĩwasembie asyoka kĩthekanĩ vala watiĩte mwendwa wake. Ĩndĩ ndamwĩthĩa. Nĩwamwĩtie kwa ĩsyitwa na wasya mũnene, ĩndĩ nĩkwethĩiwe kĩvindyo kĩnene. Na ĩndĩ niwew'ie wasya ũkyasya, "wĩtana nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ũtesĩ wĩkĩthekanĩ kya Mũsambwa wa Limbeeletwela?"
eng: He hurried back to the forest to where he had left his newfound darling. But she was nowhere to be seen. He called her name very loudly, but there was complete silence. Then he heard a voice saying, "Why are you calling? Don't you know that you are in the forest area of Musambwa kwa Libeeletwela?"

kam: Tene tene vyũ kwaĩ mũndũ ũmwe ngya na mũka wake. Maĩna kana kamwe ka kelĩtu ketawa Nokũngũ. Nokũngũ aĩ mwanake na mũthingu. Asyai make nĩmamwendete mũno.
eng: Once upon a time there was a poor man and his wife. They had only one child, a girl. The child's name was Nonkungu. Her parents loved Nonkungu very much.

kam: Mũthenya ũmwe asyai make nĩmavangie kũmũtwaa kwa naũme wake mũthui wetawa Mũtonyama. Inya nĩwamũseũvĩsye kĩsikati kĩseo kĩna malaa na ivungo na wanyũa. Nĩwamũseũvĩsye ĩsoa ya wanyũa na ĩndĩ amũtũma ndũanĩ ya naũme.
eng: One day her parents decided to send her to stay with her rich Uncle Mtonyama. Nonkungu's mother made a special skirt with ribbon, buttons and beads. She also made a beautiful bead necklace for Nonkungu. Then she sent her off to her uncle's village.

kam: Aendete Nokũngũ nĩwethĩie kalũsĩ na akakĩla akinyangĩte mavia. Mũingo Nokũngũ nĩwakomanie na kelĩtu kanini kekĩte ilai.
eng: On the way Nonkungu came to a stream. She crossed the stream using the stepping stones. On the other side she met a young girl wearing rags.

kam: Kelĩtu nĩkamũkũlilye, "Wendete kũ?" "Nendete kũkethya mama Mũtonyama," Nokũngũ nĩwasũngĩie "Onakwa Mũtonyama nĩ mama na nendete kũmũkethya," kelĩtu nĩkaisye. Kwou nĩmatembeie vamwe.
eng: "Where are you going?" asked the young girl. "I'm going to visit my Uncle Mtonyama," said Nonkungu. "Well, Mtonyama is my uncle, too and I am also on my way to visit him," said the young girl. So they walked on together.

kam: Mendanga vanini kelĩtu nĩkaisye, "kĩsikati kyaku nĩkĩseo mũno na ĩsoa yaku nĩyanake, vatonyeka nenge nele." Nokũngũ nĩwaumisye kĩsikati na ĩsoa yake na anenge kala kelĩtu.
eng: Before they had gone very far, the young girl said, "Your skirt is so beautiful and your beads are so pretty. Please let me try them on." So Nonkungu took off her skirt and beads and gave them to the young girl.

kam: Ĩla kelĩtu kau kaumisye ilai syako nakekĩa ngũa sya Nokũngũ, Nokũngũ nĩwonie kelĩtu kena mwĩthe! Nokũngũ nĩwew'ie w'ĩa nũndũ nĩwamanyie kelĩtu kau nĩyalyũka.
eng: When the girl took off her rags and changed into Nonkungu's clothes, Nonkungu saw that the young girl had a tail! Nonkungu was afraid. She knew now that the young girl was really an imbulu.

kam: Nĩmatembeangie vamwe na Nokũngũ asya, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa." Ĩndĩ yalyũka nĩyaisye, "eka nĩkĩange nginya tũvike mũtĩnĩ ũya." Nĩyaolotile mũtĩ wĩ kĩĩmanĩ.
eng: They walked on together. "Please give me back my skirt and my beads," asked Nonkungu. But the imbulu answered, "Let me wear them until we get to that tree." She pointed to a tree on the hill.

kam: Ĩla mavikĩĩe mũtĩ ũsu, Nokũngũ nĩwaisye, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa." "Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kalũsĩnĩ kala katĩe," yalyũka nĩyaisye. Nokũngũ nĩwetĩkĩlile nũndũ nĩwakĩaa.
eng: When they reached the tree, Nonkungu said to the imbulu, "Please give me back my skirt and beads." "Just let me wear them until we get to the next stream," said the imbulu. Nonkungu was afraid, so she agreed.

kam: Nĩmavikie kala kalũsĩnĩ na Nokũngũ eea yalyũka, "vatonyeka ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa." "Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kanyũmbanĩ kaala vala iveti isu syile nthĩ," yalyũka nĩyaisye. Kwou nĩmaendie na mbee.
eng: At last they reached the stream. Again Nonkungu asked the imbulu, "Please give me back my skirt and my beads." "Just let me wear them until we get to that hut where the women are sitting," said the imbulu. So they walked on.

kam: Ĩla mavikie kanyũmbanĩ yalyuka nĩyalutile Nokũngũ ĩtina na yeya iveti ila syaile vau, "syisyai kelĩtu kaa kekĩte ilai. Kambatĩe mũthenya mũima na nenda kasyoke." Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe ni nzoni na asemba evitha kyũũnĩ.
eng: When they reached the hut, the imbulu pushed Nonkungu back and called to the women sitting by the hut. "Look at this girl wearing rags. She has been following me all day. I wish she would go away," said the imbulu. Nonkungu was so ashamed and so frightened that she ran hid in the kraal.

kam: Yalyũka nĩyendie nyũmbanĩ ya Mũtonyama na yamwĩa "ninyie mwĩvau Nokũngũ. Asyai makwa mambĩie nũke kwĩkala naku." Mũtonyama nĩwathokisye mwĩĩtu ũsu na andũ make mekala nesa na ũthingu na ĩla yalyuka. Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ ekalaa kyũũnĩ na kũya lĩu wa ngitĩ.
eng: Then the imbulu went to Uncle Mtonyama's hut. She said sweetly, "I am your niece, Nonkungu. My parents sent me to stay with you." Mtonyama welcomed the young girl. He and his family were very kind to the imbulu. But poor Nonkungu had to sleep in the kraal and share the dog's food.

kam: Kwi mũthenya Nokũngũ endaa mũũndanĩ akwĩvitha mbembanĩ na akw'ina: "Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie. Natũmiwe nĩ tata na inya nũke kwĩkala na mama Mũtonyama. Nzĩanĩ nakomanie na yalyũka na yoosa kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa. Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie."
eng: During the day Nonkungu went to the fields, hid in the corn, and sang: "Oh misery me, misery me. I was sent by my father and mother to stay with my Uncle Mtonyama. On the way I met an imbulu and she took my skirt and my beads. Oh misery me, misery me."

kam: Mũthenya ũmwe mwanainyaa Mũtonyama ũmwe akĩtembea mĩundanĩ nĩwew'ie wathi ũsu mũseo na wa tei. Ndamanya vala wathi ũsu waumaa ĩndĩ avika mũsyĩ nĩwatavisye Mũtonyama ndeto sya wathi ũsu. Mũtonyama ew'a ũu nĩwendie mũũndanĩ na.
eng: One day, one of Mtonyama's brothers was walking in the fields. He heard the strange and beautiful song. He didn't know who was singing, but when he got home, he told Mtonyama the words. Mtonyama went into the fields. He heard the song, and looked until he found Nonkungu.

kam: Nokũngũ nĩwamũtavisye ũndũ kwekĩkie, ũndũ yalyũka yamũvenie ngũa syake nzeo na yatumwa ekĩa ilai. Mũtonyama nĩwamwosie na athi nake kwake nake na amũvitha nyũmba nzĩnĩ. Mũtonyama nĩwesĩ ũndũ ũkũkwatya yalyũka.
eng: Nonkungu told him what had happened, how the imbulu had taken her beautiful clothes. Mtonyama took her back to his place and hid her in a hut. Mtonyama knew what he was going to do to catch the imbulu.

kam: Mũtonyama nĩwew'ĩte kana mwĩthe wa yalyũka nĩwendete ĩia na ndwamba kũtia ĩia ũtanywĩte ĩmwe. Kwou nĩwatavisye aũme make masimbe ĩima ĩnene na makwĩyusũsya na ĩia ĩwaatu. Nĩwetie eĩtu onthe ma ndũa moke masindane kũtwĩla.
eng: Mtonyama had heard that an imbulu's tail loves milk and that it can't go past milk without drinking some. So he told his men to dig a deep ditch and to fill the ditch with sour milk. Then he called all the girls of the village to take part in a jumping competition.

kam: Mwĩĩtu ũla wekĩĩte ngũa sya Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩthikii. Ndendaa kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩla ĩima nũndũ nĩwesĩ mwĩthe wake ũkew'a waũni wa ĩia. Kwou nĩwalikile nyũmba na oveanĩsya mwĩthe na mwĩĩ wake alũmya ũndũ vatonyeka. Na ĩndĩ nĩwendie kũlikana na eĩtu ala angĩ.
eng: The imbulu was worried. She did not want to jump over the ditch. She knew that her tail would be thirsty for the sour milk. So she went into a hut and tied her tail to her body as tightly as she could. Then she took her place with the other girls.

kam: Eĩtu nĩmanzie kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩima ũmwe ĩtina wa ũngĩ. Ĩla ĩvinda ya yalyũka yavikie nĩyatatie kũtwĩla ĩla ĩima ĩndĩ mwĩthe wayo nĩwathalĩkile waĩkusya, waĩkusya, waĩkusya, mũvaka ĩla ĩianĩ ĩwatu.
eng: One girl after another jumped over the ditch. At last it was the imbulu's turn. She tried to jump high over the ditch, but her tail broke loose. The imbulu's tail pulled her down, down, down into the sour milk.

kam: Yalyũka yendee na kwilita ĩianĩ ĩsu ĩwatu aũme nĩmosũisye ĩima na kĩthangathĩ na mathika yalyũka. Na ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũthya wa yalyũka. Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ nĩwekalile nesa na naũme kwa kĩlungu kĩasa. Ngewa yathelela vau.
eng: As the imbulu struggled in the sour milk, the men quickly filled the ditch with sand and buried her. That was the end of the imbulu. Nonkungu stayed happily with her uncle for a long, long time. And that is the end of the story.

kam: Kyumwa kithelu nina kwatie valua mbiingi.
eng: Last week I received a lot of letters.

kam: Wakwambililya ndakitali wakwa niwandikiie mwalimu wakwa valua.
eng: On Monday my doctor wrote a letter to my teacher.

kam: Thabisile ni muwau. Ngonginya ekale musyi.
eng: Thabisile is sick. She must stay at home.

kam: Wakeli ninakwatie valua kuma kilasini kyakwa.
eng: On Tuesday I got a letter from my class.

kam: Voa mituki, Thabisile!
eng: Get well soon Thabisile!

kam: Wakatatu ninakwatie value kuma kwa munyanyawa wakwa.
eng: On Wednesday I got a letter from my best friend.

kam: Nisolile ivisa yii nundu waku. Wendo kuma kwa Dudu.
eng: I drew this picture for you. Love from Dudu.

kam: Wakana ninakwatie valua kuma kwa mama.
eng: On Thursday I got a letter from my mother.

kam: Niki mwana ukuia?
eng: Why is the baby crying?

kam: Nikwathya ena nzaa.
eng: I think she is hungry.

kam: Niki kivisi ni kithatu?
eng: Why is the boy sad?

kam: Nikwatya kina mea ma ithe.
eng: I think he is missing his father.

kam: Niki kelitu ni katanu?
eng: Why is the girl happy?

kam: Kena ilinda yeu.
eng: She has a new dress.

kam: Niki mutumia mukuu ukutheka?
eng: Why is the old man laughing?

kam: Nusomie kindu kya uthekya.
eng: He read a good joke.

kam: Niki mundu muka ukukenyeesya itheka?
eng: Why is the lady smiling?

kam: Niki mundu muka ukukenyeesya itheka?
eng: Her children are reading quietly.

kam: Mundu muka ew'a ata?
eng: What is this lady feeling?

kam: Nikwatya ewa nzoni.
eng: I think she is feeling shy.

kam: Ũũ ni Ngi.
eng: This is Mr Fly.

kam: Ũũ nĩ mũtwe mũnene.
eng: This is Mr Big Head.

kam: Ngi and Mũtwe mũnene maĩ ndũũ. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩmaendie kũtembea.
eng: Mr Big Head and Mr Fly were friends. One day, they went for a walk together.

kam: Ngi nĩwaisye, "we twĩla!" "Aiee, we twĩla mbee," Mũtwe mũnene nĩwaisye. Kwou Ngi nĩwolũkile akĩla ũsĩ ũsu.
eng: Then Mr Big Head jumped into the river. But his head was so big that he started to sink.

kam: Mũtwe mũnene nĩwatwĩlie ũsĩnĩ. Ĩndĩ nũndũ mũtwe wake waĩ mũnene ndaalela; nĩwanzĩĩe kw'indanw'a nĩ kĩw'ũ.
eng: Mr Fly laughed, "Hee hee!" But he laughed so much that his mouth tore in two from one side to the other!

kam: Sũsũ aĩ vakuvĩ mĩaka mĩongo mwonza. Aĩ mũthangaau. Mũũndanĩ kwake avandaa mũvya, mwee, manga na maiũ. Sũsũ akethaa maiũ kĩla ĩvinda ya mwaka. Grandma's garden was wonderful full of sorghum, millet, and cassava. But best of all were the bananas. Although Grandma had many grandchildren, I secretly knew that I was her favourite. She invited me often to her house. She also told me little secrets. But there was one secret she did not share with me: where she ripened bananas.
eng: Grandma's garden was wonderful, full of sorghum, millet, and cassava. But best of all were the bananas. Although Grandma had many grandchildren, I secretly knew that I was her favourite. She invited me often to her house. She also told me little secrets. But there was one secret she did not share with me: where she ripened bananas.

kam: Sũsũ aĩna syana mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ katĩka onthe, nyie na aamwaiya na eetwiya kwa kĩmbithĩ nĩtwesĩ sũsũ nũtwendete kũvĩta ala angĩ. Nau nĩwe waĩ ĩlumaita ya sũsũ kwou sũsũ atũkua kwa nzĩa ya mwanya. Kwa ngelekany'o nĩwokaa mũsyĩ kwitũ mavinda maingĩ. Ĩla ena nau na mwaitũ nĩmathekaa mũno. Na kĩngĩ nowatwĩtaa nyũmba kwake mavinda maingĩ. Ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ syonthe sũsũ nĩwatũtavasyaa syĩmbithĩ syake ĩndĩ ve kĩmbithĩ kĩmwe ũtatũtavya: vala waindĩa maiũ make. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnonie kĩkavũ kya malala kiĩtwe suanĩ nza wa nyũmba ya sũsũ. Ĩla nakũlilye nĩ kyakĩ nanengiwe ũsũngĩo ũmwe kana nĩ kĩkavũ kya syama. Sũsũ anzũngĩa ou nĩwendee kũalyũla kĩtembe kya
eng: One day I saw a big straw basket placed in the sun outside Grandma's house. When I asked what it was for, the only answer I got was, "It's my magic basket." Next to the basket, there were several banana leaves that Grandma turned from time to time. I was curious. "What are the leaves for, Grandma?" I asked. The only answer I got was, "They are my magic leaves."

kam: Matukũ elĩ mathela sũsũ aĩna mĩtũkĩ ya kũthi mũkutano ndũanĩ. Nĩwandũmie ngamwosee ndata yake lumunĩ ya kũkoma. Ĩla navingũie mwango wa lumu ĩsu nĩnathokiswe nĩ muuke wa maiũ makwĩw'a.
eng: Two days later, Grandma sent me to fetch her walking stick from her bedroom. As soon as I opened the door, I was welcomed by the strong smell of ripening bananas. In the inner room was grandma's big magic straw basket. It was well hidden by an old blanket. I lifted it and sniffed that glorious smell.

kam: Lumunĩ ya nzĩnĩ ĩũsũĩte syĩndũ sya sũsũ nĩvo vaĩna kĩla kĩkavũ kya sũsũ kya syama kĩvĩthĩtwe nĩ ĩvula ĩkũũ. Nĩnavwĩkũie ĩvula na muuke wa maiũ wongelekela. Wasya wa sũsũ nĩwandelemilye akwasya, "wĩka ata we? Ngalatĩle ndata yakwa." Nĩnamũsembeesye ndata na angũlya, "nĩ kyaũ ukwetye kwenyea kũtheka?" Ĩkũlyo yake nĩyatumiswe ngũmanya kana nonendee kwenyeea ĩtheka nũndũ wa kũmanya vala vandũ va syama.
eng: Grandma's voice startled me when she called, "What are you doing? Hurry up and bring me the stick." I hurried out with her walking stick. "What are you smiling about?" Grandma asked. Her question made me realise that I was still smiling at the discovery of her magic place.

kam: Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe sũsũ ooka kũnena na mwaitũ nĩnosie kamwanya ka kũsemba nyũmbanĩ kwake ngasisye maiũ ĩngĩ. Vaĩ kĩtembe kĩmwe kyew'ĩte vyũ. Nĩnaumisye ĩiũ ĩmwe na navitha ĩlindanĩ. Natũngĩa kĩla kĩndũ nĩnasyokie nyũmba na naya ĩiũ yakwa na mĩtũkĩ. Ndyaya ĩiũ yany'a mũyo ũu ĩngĩ!
eng: The following day when grandma came to visit my mother, I rushed to her house to check the bananas once more. There was a bunch of very ripe ones. I picked one and hid it in my dress. After covering the basket again, I went behind the house and quickly ate it. It was the sweetest banana I had ever tasted.

kam: Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe nĩnetelile sũsũ athi kuuna mboka nasemba kũsisya ala maiũ. Vakuvĩ onthe nĩmew'ĩte. Ndyenamba kũmĩĩsya kũlea kwosa. Nĩnosie ana na nekalata kuumala nolwa kũvwĩka kĩkavũ.
eng: The following day, when grandma was in the garden picking vegetables, I sneaked in and peered at the bananas. Nearly all were ripe. I couldn't help taking a bunch of four. As I tiptoed towards the door, I heard grandma coughing outside. I just managed to hide the bananas under my dress and walked past her.

kam: Nuumalĩte kavola na mĩthya ya syaa sya maaũ Nĩnew'ie sũsũ akũkoa vu nza. Nĩnatatie kũvitha maiũ asu ĩlindanĩ. Namina kũya nĩnasyokie na wethĩa sũsũ ndanamanya mĩvango yakwa. Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe waĩ wa ndũnyũ. Sũsũ nĩwokĩlile tene nũndũ kĩla wa ndũnyũ nĩwatwaa maiũ meu na manga kũta. Ndyekalata kũthi kũmũkethya mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ ndyenamba kũmwĩvitha kĩlungu kyaasa.
eng: The following day was market day. Grandma woke up early. She always took ripe bananas and cassava to sell at the market. I did not hurry to visit her that day. But I could not avoid her for long.

kam: Masaa ma wĩyoo ĩla netiwe nĩ mwaitũ na nau na sũsũ nĩneesĩ kĩla ngwĩtĩwa. Ũtukũ ngũkoma nĩneesĩ kana ndikang'ea kĩndũ kya sũsũ kana kya asyai makwa kana kya mũndũ ũngĩ.
eng: Later that evening I was called by my mother and father, and Grandma. I knew why. That night as I lay down to sleep, I knew I could never steal again, not from grandma, not from my parents, and certainly not from anyone else.

kam: Ivinda ya tene kwai mundu wai na kila kindu – muunda munou, wai na ngombe, malondu na mbui. Na aendee na ukua andeea kwithiwa na kimako, nundu ndai na kindu kimwe. Ndai muka.
eng: Once upon a time, there lived a man who had plenty of everything – a large fertile farm, with cattle, sheep, and goats. But, as he grew old, he grew sad, because one thing was missing. He did not have a wife.

kam: Aungamite ungu wa muti muthenya umwe aukiwa ni ivindisya iseo. Kethiwa ndona kiveti ai atonya usovya kimwe?
eng: Standing under a tree one day, he had a brilliant idea. If he couldn't find a wife, perhaps he could make one?

kam: Kwou ambia kuseuvya kiveti kyanake kumana na uvonge wa muti. Ila waminie kuseuvya ivisa, akita metho mayo na mavinguka. Aivevea na yethiwa na thayu.
eng: So he set to work to shape a beautiful woman from a strong branch of the tree. When he had finished making the statue, he touched her eyes, and they opened. He blew gently on her, and she came alive.

kam: Kwaw'o kyai kiveti kyanake utakyona vandu vangi. Atulya ndu mbee wakyo to akikulya ethiwe mume wakyo.
eng: She was truly the most beautiful woman he had ever seen. He knelt before her, and asked her to be his wife.

kam: Akinenga ngua nzeo, wanyua na mbete ya mutwe kwonanya kyai kiveti kitwae. Na akyakia nyumba ya ndaka na nyeki ila yai vakuvi na kitina kya muti vala kyaumie. "Nikukulya kindu kimwe kwatei". Atavya kiveti kyake. "Ndukaatate utavya mundu vala waumie".
eng: He gave her a colourful apron, beads, and a head ring, the sign of a married woman. And he built her a house with the mud and grass that used to lie at the foot of her trunk. "Only one thing I beg of you," he said to his wife. "Never tell anyone where you come from."

kam: Kwa kavinda kavuthu, aume ma muika kuma utuini ungi mambiia kuneena. "Mundu mukuu ta usu atonya kwithiwa na kiveti kya muika kyanake uu ata? Mavanga kukyosa na kukitwaa kyuuni kyoo".
eng: But before long, the young men from a neighbouring village began talking among themselves. "How can such an old man have such a beautiful young wife?" So they decided to steal her and take her to their own kraal.

kam: Mukuu uu niwethiwe na kyeva muno. Ndai atonya kwikala thayu atena kiveti kiu. Ateo avindisya yingi, "Ethiwa nina kindu kyake ndyaile ni kumaka". Kwou atuma mavui, kukimantha, kukinia, na kumwetee o kindu kuma kwakyo.
eng: The old man was heartbroken. He felt he could not live without her. But then he thought, "Perhaps if I have something of hers, I would not feel so sad?" So he sent his doves to find her, to sing to her, and to bring back something of hers to him.

kam: Ila makyonie, makiniie kwa kithyomo kya nyunyi. Kiveti kya muti kiveti kya muti, Kiseo kitemoneka. Mwimiu nututumie tumutungie ngua yaku.
eng: When they found her, they sang to her in the language of birds: Tree woman, tree woman More beautiful than any other Your husband has sent us To bring back your apron!

kam: Kya manenga ngua yakyo, na mauluka iulu wa iima, mbusi, maendete kula kwi muume wakyo. Akwatie ngua yakyo vakuvi na uthyu na eewa muyo vanini.
eng: She gave them her apron, and they flew over the hill, over the river, back to her husband. He held the apron to his face, and was comforted for a little while.

kam: Wendi wake uyathela mituki. Niwatumiie mavui ingi makinie. Kiveti kya muti, kiveti kya muti kiseo kitemoneka, mwimiu nututumie tumutungie mbete yaku ya mutwe.
eng: But his longing did not go away. So again he sent his doves to sing to her: Tree woman, tree woman More beautiful than any other Your husband has sent us To bring back your head ring! And back they flew with the head ring, the sign of a married woman.

kam: Akwete mbete ya mutwe athumuuka nundu wa kiveti kyake kikuasa kyuuni kya andu angi. Kwa kavinda, eeta mavui make ingi. Thyiuuthi kula kii mukaine, kiveti kya muti kiveti kya muti kiseo kitemoneka muimiu niatutumie tumutungie thayu wake!
eng: He held the head ring and sighed for his wife, far away in the kraal of other people. After a while, he called his doves again. He told them to go to her and sing: Tree woman, tree woman More beautiful than any other Your husband has sent us To bring back your life!

kam: Kwou mathi ivinda ya katatu. Mavuila ituoni syakyo. Mainite, kila isuni yatonga itho mituki kyatwika ivisa. Maau na moko mavaluka na mutwe. Na kyavaluka muthangani.
eng: So away they went the third time. They perched on her shoulders. As they sang, each bird pecked out an eye. Immediately she turned again into a statue. Her feet and arms fell away. Then her head. And she fell to the ground.

kam: Kavola muume avingilitya kitina kya muti usini. Akyungamya na mii yakyo kiwuni. Nundu wa isua na muthanga, kyamesya matu ingi.
eng: Her husband slowly rolled her wooden trunk to the river. He stood her up with her roots in the water. Nourished by sun and soil, she grew leaves again.

kam: Na ukungi wikwo matu nimaumasya wasya. Otondu kiveti kikaa kikwenda muume.
eng: And when the wind blows, the leaves sigh. Just as a woman does when she longs for her husband.

kam: Mavika kwisho wa kyaloi,Ndeleva amea maive tikiti.Ng'ombe aiva tikiti wake.
eng: When Sakima was three years old, he fell sick and lost his sight. Sakima was a talented boy.

kam: Ndeleva athata muno.Atwaa ngali atanatungia Ngiti mbesa sya yuulu.
eng: Sakima loved to sing songs. One day his mother asked him, "Where do you learn these songs from, Sakima?"

kam: Ni kwio kitumi ona umunze Ngiti usembea ngali akunikile nzini aimaza Ndeleva ula utamutungia mbesa syake sya yuulu.
eng: Sakima answered, "They just come, mother. I hear them in my head and then I sing."

kam: Mbui nake asembaa aitoloka muumo wa ngali.Ethia aikia ndakakwatwe nundu wa ulea iva tikiti wake.
eng: Sakima liked to sing for his little sister, especially, if she felt hungry. His sister would listen to him singing his favourite song. She would sway to the soothing tune.

kam: Na Ng'ombe ndatelemaa ngali yukite.Ng'ombe osaa ivinda yake kukilanilia nzia nundu niwaivie tikiti wake wonze!
eng: "Can you sing it again and again, Sakima," his sister would beg him. Sakima would accept and sing it over and over again.

kam: Twaumaaluka tusembete. "Tuthii usini" Loreto atutavya. "Vau ni vathithangu." "Indi Mme atwia twikativie usini" Bontle atutavya " Tuyitivia" Leroto asungia. "Tuthauke munyini vakuvi na kiwu."
eng: "Bontle and Mpho and Lerato, go out and play!" Mme said to us. "I don't want you under my feet." We ran out of the house.

kam: Ateo ithau ya 'libeke' ni ivyu ona ethiwa wi ungu wa miti vakuvi na usi. Mbee twaumya syaatu. Indi twai o avyu. Twaumya sati na sikati. Indi twai o avayu.
eng: "Let's go to the river," Lerato said. "It's cooler there." "But Mme told us not to swim in the river," said Bontle. "We won't swim," answered Lerato. "We'll just play in the shade next to the water."

kam: "Inywi nenyu! Tutiviei" Asya Mpho. "Mme ndakamanya" Twativia na twativia nginya twolwa ni ivinda.
eng: We put our feet in the river to cool off. Then we splashed each other. Soon we were soaked with water.

kam: Sua yambiia kuthua na twambiia kwiwa mbevo ngua situ syaiva?
eng: "Oh come on! Let's swim," said Mpho. "Mme will never know." We swam and swam and forgot about the time.

kam: Twamantha ungu wa miti. Twamantha kithekani Twamantha kila vandu.
eng: The sun started to go down, and the day began to cool. Where were our clothes?

kam: Ateo vai ngombe syai vakuvi na usi sikuya nyeki syai muyo. Bontle asisya iulu! " Sisya ngombe iya! Yumite kyau? "Iya ilaa itune" Lerato asya."
eng: We looked under the trees. We looked on the bushes. We looked everywhere.

kam: "Ti ilaa itune" Mpho atulya wasya. "Ni sati yaku" Twasisya ngombe ingi yutanyuka kindu ki mbuluu. "Isu ni skati yakwa" Bontle atulya wasya.
eng: There were some cows near the river, enjoying the sweet grass. Bontle looked up, "Look at that cow! What's in her mouth?" "She's eating a red flower," said Lerato. "It's not a red flower," shouted Mpho. "It's your shirt!"

kam: Twenukie na ngua sya nthini tutetema nikwithiwa kwai na uthithu. "Ni ngombe" Twasya, ngombe nisyosyaie ngua situ Mme niwatwikiiie? Mituki itimba situ syavyuva. Na ti undu wa isua.
eng: We looked at another cow who was chewing something blue. "That's my skirt!" shouted Bontle.

kam: Mui umeaa mbee.
eng: The root grows first.

kam: Umeaa ulikite muthangani.
eng: It grows down into the soil.

kam: Na indi kitina kyumea kimeaa kyelekele sua.
eng: Then the stem grows. It grows up towards the sun.

kam: Matu ma mbee makumila.
eng: The first leaves come out.

kam: Mumea wa mboso uyaasava.
eng: The bean plant grows tall.

kam: Na ukyumya malaa. Malaa mautwika mboso.
eng: Then the flowers come out. The flowers turn into beans.

kam: Ve mbeu mbingi nthini wa muthande wa mboso.
eng: There are lots of seeds in the bean.

kam: Vau tene, vai iimu ika. Muthenya umwe yiitembea vakuvi na iia niyonie twilitu tutatu tunini. Yatukulya "nuu kati wenyu wendetwe ni asyai onthe.
eng: Once upon a time there was a female giant. As she was walking near the lake one day, she found three little girls. She asked them, "Who among you is loved by both parents?"

kam: Kelitu kamwe kasya "mwaitu ambendete muno" Kangi kasya "Tata ambendete muno" Kakatatu kasya, "nendetwe ni asyai onthe".
eng: One of the girls said, "My mother loves me most." Another said, "My father loves me most." But the third one said, "I am loved by both parents."

kam: Iimu yeya kelitu kala kendetwe ni asyai onthe kayaikye ngu mwongo. Kwoou kelitu katiia iimu.
eng: The giant then asked the girl loved by both parents to help her put a load of firewood on her back. So the girl followed the giant.

kam: Maendanga vanini, kelitu kakulya iimu "ngu syaku syiva" Iimu yasungia, "vakuvi na mii iyaa".
eng: After going for some distance, the girl asked the giant, "Where is your firewood?" The giant replied, "It is near those trees over there!"

kam: Mavika mitini, kelitu kakulya ingi " ngu syaku syiva?" Iimu yasungia kana mangie uvika.
eng: When they reached the trees, the girl asked again, "Where is your firewood?" The giant answered, "Not far now!"

kam: Maenda na makomana na mundu ula wakulilye iimu " kana kaku ketewa ata" Iimu yasya "Ketawa muvuko unenaa".
eng: They walked on and met a man. He asked the giant, "What is the name of your child?" The giant replied, "She is called the 'talking bag'."

kam: Kelitu katheka muno na kaina Tinye muvuko unenaa Nitawa Kaamungei Uui mwaitu numbendete Uui – tata numbendete Ui, kikuu kyakwa Ninywiaa iia.
eng: The girl burst out singing: "I am not called the talking bag. My name is Kaamungei! Oh! My mother, whom I love, Oh! My father, whom I love, Oh! My calabash, which I use to drink milk!"

kam: Ila mundu wewei kelitu undu kaina, akataanany'a na akatungia asyai mako. Ukewa wathelela vau!
eng: When the man heard what the girl sang, he rescued her and took her back to her parents. The story ends there!

kam: Ivinda ya tene, tene vyu, vee mbuavui weetawa Anansi. Kiveti kya Anansi kyai muui museo. Ateo kila ivinda, Anansi niwendaa weuni kusamasama liu ula andu utuini mayauaa vamwe na misyi yoo.
eng: Once upon a time, there was a spider called Anansi. He was too lazy to cook his own food. Instead, he used to visit his friends and eat the delicious food they had cooked.

kam: Muthenya umwe avitila kwa Mbaluku. Kavaluku ai munyanyae. "Ve mboka mbisuni" Anansi aneena ewite muyo. Anansi "syinamba kuvya" kavaluku amutavya, "ateo nisyuvya mituki, eteela tuye vamwe". "Nindonya kwendeew'a ateo nina syindu ngwika," Anansi asya na mituki. Ukethia etelile ethiwa aneewa wia eke ni kavaluku.
eng: One day, he was walking past Rabbit's house when he smelled something cooking. "Greens!" he said excitedly. "They're not quite ready yet," said Rabbit. "You can help me with the washing up in the mean time." "Sorry, I have things to do. I'll come back later," said Anansi.

kam: "Ninisi" Anansi aweta. "Ningwaka ulwalui. "Ningwovea ulwalui umwe kuuni kwakwa na ungi mbisuni yake, liu wavya kusya ulwalui umwe na ninguka nzembete!" Mbaluku oona uu ni useo na awika.
eng: "How will I call you when they're ready?" asked Rabbit. Anansi thought for a minute. "I'll spin a web," he said, "and tie one end around my leg and one end to your pot. When the greens are ready, pull on the web string and I'll come right away." So Anansi tied the web to the pot, and walked on.

kam: "Ningwiw'a mboso syunyunga," Anansi aneena atembeete. "Mboso syina muyo, syi mbisuni syuvya." Uka tuye mboso situ", makuli mamutavya."syangiie kuvya.". "Nindonya kwendeew'a Tata nguli," Anansi asya. Na ingi asya ni ukuseuvya ulwalui na oveye umwe kuuni na uungi wovewe mbisuni nene ya mboso. Tata Nguli niwoonie kana uu wai useo na awika.
eng: A short while later he saw Monkey and his wife, cooking some beans in a large pot. "Come and join us!" they said. "The beans are nearly ready." "Sorry, I have things to do," said Anansi before they could ask him to help. "But let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the beans are ready, pull on the web string, and I'll come."

kam: "Niwa makwasi mainyunga" Anansi aneena ena muyo atembeete. " Makwasi na uki wa nzuki, ningwisilya. "Anansi", munyanyae kithangaite amwita. "Mbisu yakwa yusuite makwasi na uki wa nzuki! Uka tuisanie" "Nonendeewe" Anansi na ingi asya nukuseuvya ulwalui na umwe wovewe kuuni kwake na muthia ungi wovew'e mbisuni ya makwasi. Munyanyae kithangaiti oona uu ni useo na eeka w'o.
eng: He walked on until he smelled sweet potatoes. "Anansi," called his friend Warthog. "My pot is full of sweet potatoes and honey! Come and share my food with me. Here's a fork for you to help me stir." "I'll come back later," said Anansi quickly. "But let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the sweet potatoes are ready, pull on the web string, and I'll come."

kam: Ivinda ila Anansi wavikie usini aina ulwalui wovewe mau make nyanya. "Uu ni undu u useo" Anansi aiya ena muyo. "Ndyisi ni mbisu yau ikuvya mbee. O saa isu Anansi eewa ulwalui umwe wakitwa. "Oo", Anansi atumua, "Usu ni ulwalui ula wovewe mbisuni ya mboka sya mbaluku".
eng: By the time Anansi arrived at the river, each of his eight legs was tied to a different pot of delicious food. Just then, Anansi felt a tug on one of his legs. "Rabbit's food is ready!" he said, licking his lips.

kam: Anansi avingilita alika kiwuni. Ila molwalui oonthe matwaiswe ni kiwu, asyoka yingi akwiwa woo ngukani. "ai, ai, ai, ai", Anansi, avevuuka, " Nikwatya uu ndwii undu useo, ona vanini " Kuvikia umunthi mbuavui Anansi ethiwa na maau nyanya matheke muno. Na muthenya usu ndaakwata liu ona umwe.
eng: Finally, the web strings could hold no longer. They snapped one by one. Anansi rolled into the river to soothe his painful legs. But his legs would not return to their normal shape. And he was too embarrassed to go to any of his friends and share their food that day.

kam: Ĩvinda ya tene na tene, vaĩna musyĩ wekalaa na ũtanu.
eng: Once upon a time, there lived a happy family.

kam: Mayaũkitanaa ene kwa ene. Nimatetheesyaa asyai moo musyĩ na mĩundani.
eng: They never fought with each other. They helped their parents at home and in the fields.

kam: Ĩndĩ mayanengetwe mwanya wakũthi vakuvĩ na mwaki.
eng: But they were not allowed to go near a fire.

kam: Maĩlĩte kũthũkũma wĩa woo w'onthe ũtukũ. Nũndũ mĩĩ yoo yaseovetw'e na mũvũa!
eng: They had to do all their work during the night. Because they were made of wax!

kam: Ĩndĩ mwana ũmwe aĩ na mea ma kũthi nza kwĩanĩkĩa kyeni kya sua.
eng: But one of the boys longed to go out in the sunlight.

kam: Ũũi! Mwana ũsu ndaatetheka. Nĩwanyinyũkie nũndũ wa ũvyuvu wa sua.
eng: But it was too late! He melted in the hot sun.

kam: Syana sya mũvũa nĩsyakwatiwe ni kyeva nũndũ wa kwona mwanaainya ainyinyuka.
eng: The wax children were so sad to see their brother melting away.

kam: Ĩndĩ nĩmethĩiw'e na mũvango. Nĩmosie mũndo wa mũvũa ula wanyinyukie maseovya kasũni.
eng: But they made a plan. They shaped the lump of melted wax into a bird.

kam: Nĩmosie mwanaainya kasũni mamũlĩsya ĩũlu wa kĩĩma kĩtũlu.
eng: They took their bird brother up to a high mountain.

kam: Na sua ĩkuuma nĩwolũkile athi kũu akwina kyeninĩ kya kĩoko.
eng: And as the sun rose, he flew away singing into the morning light.

kam: Sipho aendete tauni na mwiitu yinya.
eng: Sipho goes to town with his sister.

kam: Mwiitu yinya wake asyaisye ngua ndukani. Sipho niuboikie.
eng: His sister is looking at the clothes in shops. Sipho is bored.

kam: Sipho asyaise kindu wivata nakyo.
eng: Sipho sees something he likes.

kam: Siatu ni kuteewa.
eng: The shoes are on sale.

kam: Aelile syonthe.
eng: He tries them all on.

kam: Mwiitu inyia wake amuyiye siatu sya muvila .
eng: His sister buys him soccer shoes.

kam: Kwa vaati nzeo alikie kiwanzani kya mauu isaani! Ekite siatu syake sya muvila wa mauu.
eng: Why are they in such a hurry to get home?

kam: Kwa ivinda iasa, Olokwango aungamite akenyesya itheka katikati wa uii wa kwene. Kuma Malong'ola eli ngali syonthe ili, vaumite mbusi ila syakomanite miandani kuseuvya usi. Usi wa Temu wavitilite uini wa Kweni ukilitye ki. Kiwu kyaw'o kyai kinengo kwa ng'ombe, matunda na mbui sya utuini ovamwe na Nzia ila yekalaa uini usu.
eng: For ages, Olokwango hill stood smiling at the middle of Kwere plains. From the two dimples on its side came springs which converged downhill to form a river. River Temu meandered silently across the Kwere plains. Its waters were a gift to the sheep and goats of the area as well as the deer that dwelt in the plains.

kam: Maundu maendee nesa muvaka ila Matata watwikie mutui. Aisye nzia niseuvwe isilite kiimani nikana alisae kiimani vate thina wa uvingilita mbika nthi kavola. Kiima kya Olokwango nikyathatie muno, nundu wa kwanangwa kwa king'ewa kyake ateo kyaumisya.
eng: Things were all well until Matata became headman. He ordered a path to be cleared from the top of the hill to the foot so that he could climb uphill easily and roll gently down to the foot. Olokwango hill was angry with the damage to his beard, but he was patient.

kam: Muthia wa kyumwa, syana sya Matata na anyangae moo nimalisaa kiimani kuthauka. Masembaa kila vandu, maitulanga mbonge sya miti, makyakany'a miaki na kumitia yakene.
eng: During the weekend, Matata's children and their friends would climb uphill to play. They would run all over the place, breaking twigs and branches, lighting fires for their games, which they would later leave burning.

kam: Kwa ivinda Olokwango anoa. Kavola aeka kukenyeesya itheka. Malong'ola maendeea na unyiva na uthyu wake waendeea na ukunzana. Mwisio ila mbusi ili syang'ala. Nguka sya usi wa Temu syasianisya kwa kimako. Nzia ila syai uini syathama nundu vayai nyeki ndaasa, ithaukia na vandu vavinyu vaukoma. Ng'ombe, mbui na malondu syamosa vyu. Kila umwe eew'a kimako kya kiima kya Olokwongo.
eng: Over time, Olokwango lost patience. The dimples became smaller and smaller as his face turned into ugly wrinkles. At last the springs were no more. The deer in the plains migrated because there was no more the tall green grass to play in. The sheep and goats grew thinner and thinner. Everyone felt the sadness of Olokwango hill.

kam: Andu ma Kwere nimamanyie kana ve kindu kikwenda kwikwa. Nimakwatanie na maumya Matata kivilani. Vandu vake manyuva Baraka ula mituki waisye kila mundu navande ilaa manenge Olokwongo ndaia. Baraka na andu make maseuvya sikuku na maete mithinzio ya miti ya maana kwa Olokwongo.
eng: The people of Kwere realized that something needed to be done. They joined hands and overthrew Matata the headman. In his place they appointed Baraka who immediately ordered everyone to plant a flower to honour Olokwango. Baraka and his people held ceremonies and brought gifts of pine, cedar, and cypress for Olokwango.

kam: Vai mundu watenbeelaa kiimani kiu na nyeki yamea yingi. Kwa kavola itheka ya kiima kya Olokwongo yaingiva na malongola malikanga. Kuma malongolani asu mbusi syaumila ingi. Usi wa Temu wathayuuka. Mbii syatwika sya kisunzuni nundu wa miti na nyeki. Nzia syambiia kusembasemba ingi ku nyekini. Ng'ombe, mbui, na malondu syathumua munyini wa miti.
eng: No one walked on the hill any longer, and the grass had a chance to grow tall once again. Gradually the smile on the face of Olokwango hill grew broader and the dimples deeper. Out of the dimples the springs ran again. River Temu was rejuvenated. The plains became greener than ever before. The deer galloped happily once more across the grass.

kam: "Ikala thayu mwasa Baraka, ikala thayu mwasa Baraka" andu ma Kwere maina. "Ikala thayu mwasa Olokwongo" Baraka na andu masya. "Syana syenyu na syana sya syana syoo na nzukulu syoo nisyunenge ndaia kila ivinda.
eng: "Long live Baraka, long live Baraka," the people of Kwere sang. "Long live, Olokwango," said Baraka and his people. "May our children and children's children forever respect you."

kam: Kayanga ekalile na asyai make nginya metwa emĩaka ĩkũmi.
eng: Khayanga lived with her parents happily until they died when she was ten years old.

kam: Kĩveti kĩmwe kya mũkonyo woo kyetawa Losa nĩkyamwosie kyathi kwĩkala nake mũsyĩ kwakyo. Losa aĩngya na mũkũũ ĩndĩ aĩmũthingu.
eng: Khayanga was taken in by Rosa, a distant relative. Rosa was kind to Khayanga, but she was old, frail and poor.

kam: Kayanga mavinda maingĩ nĩwendaa tũvulĩnĩ twa asyai make kũmatavya mathĩna make.
eng: Khayanga often visited her parents' graves to tell them of her misery.

kam: Mũthenya ũmwe ĩla Kayanga wendie kwona tũvulĩ nĩwanengiwe mũthĩnzĩo mũseo wa kĩkuu kya mwanya Kyaumĩlile tũvulĩnĩ twa asyai make.
eng: One day when she visited, she received a gift. It was a very special Gourd which appeared from her parents' graves.

kam: Kayanga akuaa kĩkuu kĩu kĩla vandu vonthe wendaa. Nũndũ wa kĩkuu kĩũ Kayanga nĩwew'aa eũsũvĩonĩ wa asyai make.
eng: Khayanga carried her special Gourd everywhere. With her Gourd, Khayanga felt her parents' presence and protection.

kam: Mũthenya ũmwe kĩndũ kĩthũku nĩkyekĩkie. Kĩkuu kyake nĩkyatũkanie ĩla wendie kũutĩa kĩw'ũ ũsĩnĩ. Kayanga nĩwew'ie ngoo yake onayo nyatũka.
eng: One day, something bad happened to her special Gourd. It broke when she was fetching water in the river. Khayanga's heart broke as well.

kam: Kayanga nĩwew'ie wasya wainya ũkĩmwĩa: Mwanawitũ, Osany'a ilungu isu syatiwa. Tava kĩw'ũ nasyo nawĩthamba maaũ. Wamina kũthamba vinga metho maku. Kayanga nĩwekie ũndũ wataviwe na kwa mĩtũkĩ ilungu isu nĩsyetungĩanĩe syasovya kĩkuu kĩima ĩngĩ.
eng: Khayanga heard her mother's voice saying to her: "Our child, pick up the pieces that are left. Fetch water with them and wash your feet. When you finish washing, close your eyes." Khayanga obeyed and suddenly, the broken Gourd became whole once again.

kam: Kayanga nĩwaendee kũkua kĩkuu kĩu kĩla vandũ waendaa. Kĩla vandũ vonthe wesĩlaa andũ nĩmaseng'aa na kũmũkũlya kĩkuu kĩu nĩkyamũthemba mwaũ nũndũ mayaona kĩngĩ ta kĩu ĩngĩ. Kĩkuu kĩu kyake nĩkyamũnengae kĩla ũkwenda.
eng: Khayanga continued to carry her Gourd everywhere she went. Wherever she passed, people whispered to each other, "What type of gourd is this?" With her special Gourd, Khayanga received everything she needed.

kam: Akwĩkala na kĩkuu kĩu kya mwanya Kayanga nĩwesĩ kana asyai make nĩmamũsũvĩaa na vaĩ kĩndũ kĩthũku kĩtonya kwĩkĩka.
eng: With the special Gourd, Khayanga knew that her parents were watching over her. Nothing bad could happen to her.

kam: Ii ni manyatta. Nivo kwitu. Nyumba yakwa yi nthini wa kisio kya Turkana.
eng: This is a Manyatta. It is my home. My home is in Turkana County.

kam: Ii ni ngamile. Nthini wa kisio kya Turkana andu nimaithasya nyamu syi kivathukany'o. Ateo ngamile ni nyamu yendekete muno.
eng: This is a camel. In Turkana County people keep many different animals. But the camel is very important.

kam: Aa ni alimu makwa. Nindete kuthi sukulu. Sukulu yakwa yitawa Lolupe. Ninendete mwalimu wakwa wa syindu sya useuvya na moko.
eng: These are my teachers. I like going to school. My school is called Lolupe Primary School. I like my Art teacher very much.

kam: Ii ni meli. Meli ni nene. Itumikaa kwa kukua andu na miio kiwuni. Ngathi Mwambasa ni kwona meli.
eng: This is a ship. Ships are big. They are used to transport people and goods on water. If I go to Mombasa, I can see a ship.

kam: Kii ni kitanda. Nau wanzeuvisye. Nikitumiaa na mwinawa wa munduume. Wiwaa nesa ukikomee.
eng: This is a bed. I like the bed that my father made for me. I share it with my younger brother. It is comfortable.

kam: Ii ni nzamba. Musyi twi nzamba ili. Na twi nguku mbiingi. Nilekasya matumbi maingi.
eng: This is a cock. At home, we have two cocks. We also have many chickens. The chickens lay many eggs.

kam: Ii ni mbia ni nyamu nzuku ni syisaa liu. Nisyanangaa ngua. Nisyetae mowau.
eng: This is a mouse. Mice are dangerous animals. They eat food. They also destroy clothes. They can cause disease.

kam: Ii ni ngiti. Ngiti ni nyamu sya musyi. Ngiti yiitu yitawa Daa. Ikumaa muno.
eng: This is a dog. Dogs are domestic animals. Our dog is called Daa. He barks a lot.

kam: Uu ni mwavuli. Asyai makwa me mwavuli munene. Wina langi mutune, mbuluu, ilaa ya muuti na kisunzuni. Ila kwina mbua, tutumiaa mwavuli twikauiwe.
eng: This is an umbrella. My parents have a big umbrella. It has red, blue, orange and green colours. When it rains, we use an umbrella so we do not get wet.

kam: Ni kilasi kya keli na ninisi syindu mbingi. Ningwenda kumanya ingi mbingi. Kila ndesi ngulasya musyai kana mwalimu.
eng: I am in class two and I know many things. I want to know many more. What I do not know, I ask my parents or my teacher.

kam: Niki itu ni mbuluu?
eng: Why is the sky blue?

kam: Ti indi yonthe yithiawa mbuluu, kana?
eng: It is not always blue. Is it?

kam: Niki matu ni kisunzuni?
eng: Why are leaves green?

kam: Maithiawa me kisunzuni mavinda onthe. Kana?
eng: They are not always green. Are they?

kam: Niki maiu ni ilaa ya muuti?
eng: Why are bananas yellow?

kam: Maiu meu mélangi wa ilaa ya muuti. Maiu methi me langi wa kusunzuni.
eng: Ripe bananas are yellow. Unripe bananas are green.

kam: Niki myavuli ni nziu?
eng: Why are umbrellas black?

kam: Myavuli yonthe ti nziu.
eng: Not all umbrellas are black.

kam: Niki nthakame ni ndune?
eng: Why is blood red?

kam: Ve kindu nthakameni kila kimitwikithasya ndune.
eng: There is iron in the blood. That makes it red.

kam: Niki munyu ni mweu?
eng: Why is salt white?

kam: Ndyisi.
eng: I don't know!

kam: Mzi ekalaa nyumba ya musonge.
eng: Mzi lives in a thatched house.

kam: Thulani ekalaa nyumbani ya kona inya sianene.
eng: Thulani lives in a square house.

kam: Nyumba ii ni ya kona inya iteanene.
eng: This house is a rectangle.

kam: Wite wa nyumba ii ni wa kona itatu.
eng: The roof of this house is a triangle.

kam: Mundu uu eaka nyumba yake.
eng: This man is building his own house.

kam: Nyumba ii ni nzeu.
eng: This house is new.

kam: Nyumba ii ni nguu.
eng: This house is old.

kam: Kethiwa no nekalie nyumba ii.
eng: I wish I lived in this house.

kam: Mbaka nikwataa mbia.
eng: Cats catch mice.

kam: Huu niw'o usi wa katatu munene nduniani.
eng: This is the third longest river in the world.

kam: Mwaitu atũmie valũa hũũ kwacha.
eng: My grandmother posted the letter this morning.

kam: Nuthambisye ngali?
eng: Have you washed the car yet?

kam: Niniendete ngiti.
eng: I like dogs.

kam: Ũvoo!
eng: Hello!

kam: Ngiti nisyiukuma.
eng: Dogs are barking.

kam: Mbaka hĩĩ nĩ yakwa.
eng: This is my cat.

kam: Tom niwe munene waku.
eng: Tom is your boss.

kam: Ngali ya mwaki isovetw'e na ngali mũonza.
eng: The train is made up of seven cars.

kam: wakwambiliilya, anasayanzi kuma sukulu wa stanford wa dawa matangaasie kuseuvya kwa muio mweu wa kuthima ula utonya kuvathukanya cell na muvae : kachip kaini katonya uprinitiwa kala katonya usoovwa kutumia printa ya inkjet standard kwa centi imwe ya U.S.
eng: On Monday, scientists from the Stanford University School of Medicine announced the invention of a new diagnostic tool that can sort cells by type: a tiny printable chip that can be manufactured using standard inkjet printers for possibly about one U.S. cent each.

kam: Atongoi ma ũkunĩkĩli measya ũkwatĩkani wa tene wa kanza, kĩthũĩ, ũkimu na ndetema kwĩ awau ala me nthĩ syĩ ĩkya, kũla ũtonyekano wa'ũvoa wa maũwau ta kanza ya nondo noũtonye kwĩthĩwa wĩ nusu ya ala me nthĩ nthuangi.
eng: Lead researchers say this may bring early detection of cancer, tuberculosis, HIV and malaria to patients in low-income countries, where the survival rates for illnesses such as breast cancer can be half those of richer countries.

kam: Ndege kwa ĩsyĩtwa ya JAS 39C Gripen nĩyeethĩiwe na mbaga saa 9.30 sya kwakya (0230 UTC) na kũlivũka, na kũtũma vĩasala wa kũkuana na ndege kũvũngwa kĩwanzanĩ kyũ kya ndege.
eng: The JAS 39C Gripen crashed onto a runway at around 9:30 am local time (0230 UTC) and exploded, closing the airport to commercial flights.

kam: Mutwai usu wa ndeke nuikiithiw'e ta mutongoi wa ndeke isu sya kau Dilokrit Pattavee.
eng: The pilot was identified as Squadron Leader Dilokrit Pattavee.

kam: Isese sya mauvoo sya kuu syalivoti kana ngali ya kiwanzani kya ndeke yavaluka isembete ikaokoe.
eng: Local media reports an airport fire vehicle rolled over while responding.

kam: vĩdal ũla wĩna myaka 28 analĩkĩle barca mbũa itatũ mbĩtũkũ kũma sevĩlla.
eng: 28-year-old Vidal had joined Barça three seasons ago, from Sevilla.

kam: Kũma athĩ Catalan-capital, Vidal athaũkĩte mathaũ mala 49 kwa kĩkũndĩ kĩũ.
eng: Since moving to the Catalan-capital, Vidal had played 49 games for the club.

kam: Maandamano mambiie kindu saa 11:00 (UTC+1) Whitehall ila isianitye na mũomo ũsungawa ni askali wa kulika Downing Street, vala Mũsũmbi wikalaa.
eng: The protest started around 11:00 local time (UTC+1) on Whitehall opposite the police-guarded entrance to Downing Street, the Prime Minister's official residence.

kam: O ĩtina wa saa 11.00 kũvĩka, alei nĩmavingie nzĩa ngalĩko ya yĩũlũ ya Whitehall.
eng: Just after 11:00, protesters blocked traffic on the northbound carriage in Whitehall.

kam: Twi 11:20, asikali makulilye aandamani masyoke itina kwa kasila, meimea kana maila umbalanzi kwithwa na uthasyo wa kuandamana na kuvunga nzia.
eng: At 11:20, the police asked the protesters to move back on to the pavement, stating that they needed to balance the right to protest with the traffic building up.

kam: Saa ĩtano na mĩongo ĩlĩ na kenda, mũkomo ũu nĩ welekeĩle Whitehall, mbee wa Trafalgar Square, ũtee wa Strand, wavita Aldwych na wambata Kingsway welekele Holborn vala Conservative Party maina na ũmbano wa Spring Forum utelini wa Grand Connaught.
eng: Around 11:29, the protest moved up Whitehall, past Trafalgar Square, along the Strand, passing by Aldwych and up Kingsway towards Holborn where the Conservative Party were holding their Spring Forum in the Grand Connaught Rooms hotel.

kam: Lekoti ya kyongo kwa kyongo ya Nadal na Muukananda usu ni 7-2.
eng: Nadal's head to head record against the Canadian is 7–2.
