eng: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

kam: Ni matwikite me aseo muno kwa utila awau mamutha kumavonokya kuma kwa ganrene vamwe na tourniquets na mwikiva kuvunga nikenda nthakame yieke kuma.
eng: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

kam: Kwa sengyali kauta, unene wa Roman watumie ukwati munene muveani wa ndawa na weethwa na umanyi mwingi ula twisi umunthi.
eng: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

kam: Kukunza mathangu kwa pureland ni kukunza mathangu kwi miao kana no ikunza yimwe yitonya kwikwa kwa ivinda yimwe, makunza momu munango ta kukunza na itina timetikile, na makunza monthe methiawa kunduni kwenekee.
eng: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

kam: Yasooviwe ni John Smith mwaka wa 1970s itetheesye andu ala matena umanyi mwingi wa kukunza kana ala matena utonyi munene wa kuthukuma na moko.
eng: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

kam: Syana nisyambiaa umanya iulu wa mũvai wa mundu na undu uilye muvaĩ syi nini na undu uu ni uaffectiaa mwikalo wasyo.
eng: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

kam: Kwa ngelekany'o, syana ila imanyikanaa kwisila kwa muvai ula munini ula ukonanaw'a na kwithwa mate aseo sukulu mavinda maingi nimavalukaa sukulu ila mamanya kana nimakonanaw'a na undu usu wa muvai woo.
eng: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

kam: MySpace niw'o mutandao wa katatu kwa kumanyikana ku Amelika na kwa oyu wina aatiii milioni 54.
eng: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

kam: Websites ii syithwaa na undu wa kuatiiwa muno, muno muno kwa ngaliko ya kisomo.
eng: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

kam: Ve moseo ma mitandao ii, ila ni vamwe na, kwithiwa utonya kwambiisya mathangu ala ni ta mbulongo, vindio, visa, na syindu ingi mbingi.
eng: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

kam: veengyi ii noumyone kwisila kwa kunengane web andresi o imwe tu, kila kitumaa yithwa yi laisi kumililikana na ingi kuandika laisi kwa amanyiw'a ala methwa na thina wa kutumia kiimboti kana kwa kuendelesya.
eng: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

kam: No iseuvwe ni kinda withie no usome na langi mwingi kana munini undu ukwenda.
eng: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

kam: Uwau wa kuvungula kwa kwithukiisya nesa "ni uwau wa kiakili ula mawonany'o maw'o ni mbuka, kuvuavuana, na kutethya wia saa syonthe kana vinya mwingi".
eng: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

kam: Ti kuemwa nikusoma, ni uwau wa kusoma; "yikwataa syana syonthe ta vaasendi ya 3 nginya 5, noethwa no mbingi ta milioni 2 kwa syana sya Amelika".
eng: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

kam: Syana ila syina ADD ni siemawa kũtũnga ilĩko syoo wiani wa sukulu, indi ni nisyitũnga ilĩko syinduni ila syendete ika ta kuthauka na kusyiisya katuni kana kuandika ilungu syitena ikomo.
eng: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

kam: Syana isu nisyonaa thina mwingi muno. Nundu "syithaa na tavia kya muisyo munene muno, ikokita na syii tata ukumu" nikana yiamusye kiliko, nundu kiliko kiyisa kuamusywa na nzia kya kawaida.
eng: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

kam: ADD ni yanangaa undu mailenie na ala angi tondu syana ila angi syiikwatasya niki meika undu meika, undu masomaa syindu kana nundu uima woo ui kiwango kimwe.
eng: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

kam: O undu utonyi wa kukwata umanyi o vamwe na kusoma wavindukie kwa nzia o ila iwetetwe vaa yiulu o ta uu mituki ya kukwata umanyi niyavindukie.
eng: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

kam: Nzia ya kukwata uvoo yii kivathukany'o. Vai nai pressure iulu wa kila mundu kwitwa, ateo utonyi wa kulilikana utumani niw'o wai vata.
eng: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

kam: Kwa undu wa maana, ulilikano usu waetie ũalyũku wi vata kwa nzia ya usomethya na kunyaiikya ũmanyi.
eng: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

kam: Kivathukany'o na primates ila ingi, hominids nisyaekie utumia moko masyo kwa kuthi kana kukua uito kana kusua mitini.
eng: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

kam: Kw'oko na kuu kwa ilai kwithwaa kwianene nginya uasa, wonany'o mwianu kana kw'oko nikutumiawa ukua uito ila itembeete.
eng: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

kam: Kw'oko kwa mundu ni kukuvi kwi kuu, na kwii tuvindi tuungamangu.
eng: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

kam: Mawindi ala matene vyu ma myaka ta milioni ili nginya milioni itatu nimekwonany'a uvinduku wa specilization ya kw'oko kuma locomotion nginya manipulation.
eng: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

kam: Andu amwe maikiiaa kana kwithwa na ndoto sya kwitongoesya mala maingi syi minoo.
eng: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

kam: Kĩtũmĩ kĩnene kya kĩko kĩĩ nũndũ wa ũvangĩthya mũseo wa ndoto ĩla sya nenevĩsye saa katĩ wa nthĩ sya REM.
eng: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

kam: Kwithwa na REMs kila wiyoo, ivindani yii wiw'aa too mweene na mwii uyithwa na thina na kwiyiw'a.
eng: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

kam: ũũ wĩ na mĩnoo ta kũamũka ĩtina wa kĩla ndatĩka mĩongoĩ ilĩ kana mĩongo ĩtatũ wĩloele tiivii.
eng: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

kam: useo kana uthuku witengemea undu akili yaku ikwiyielesya kila utuku ndotoni.
eng: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

kam: Maundu mayaathi nesa kwa Italians ngaliko ya iulu ya Avilika kuma mwambiio. Nthini wa kyumwa kimwe Itali yatangaasa kau wa mwei wa thanthatu 1940, Hussards ma uungelesa ya 11 niyakwatite mateka Fort Capuzzo kuu Libya.
eng: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

kam: Kwisila kuthi mevithite, ngaliko ya utee ya Bardia, Asungu ni mamukwatie munene wa useuvya syindu wa jeshi ya ikumi ya Itali, General Lastucci.
eng: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

kam: Twi mwei wa wathanthatũ matuku 28, Marshall Italo Balbo, Ngavana Mũnene wa nthi ya Libya na mũtiiwa ũnene wa Mussolini, auwaiwe ni mwaki wa kiunyanya ila wevuilaa nthi kuu Tobruk.
eng: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

kam: Ithau yii yeu ya kuuta ni yithaukawa iwangoni syi kivathukanyo, kuma amanyiwa ma yunivasĩtĩ nginya ala me wiani na asembi.
eng: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

kam: Ithau ithaukawa kwa nzia ya nguthu kana andu eli, mwikii wiio umwe ayukita ula ungi.
eng: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

kam: Ngovu ni ithau yila athauki matumiaa tumiti ukuna mivila ilike maimani.
eng: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

kam: Maima ikumi na nyanya ni mathaukawa laundini imwe. Athauki mambiaa ya mbee na maiminiia ya ikumi ya nyanya.
eng: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

kam: Mũthaũki ula ukũkũna makũna manini, kana kũsũa kwa kilavu, aile umina koosi kwa kusinda.
eng: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

kam: Ithau yii yithaukiwa nyekini na nyeki ila yi vakũvi na yiima ni ndile yi ngũvi kute ila ingi na yitawa "the green".
eng: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

kam: Noethwa nzĩa ĩla yĩsĩkĩe mũno ya ũtalii noyo andũ aingĩ mamĩkwatanasya na kũtembea: ũtalii wa kũseũvya ĩngĩ.
eng: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

kam: Ĩĩ nĩ ĩla andũ maendaa vandũ ve kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na vala mekalaa kĩla mũthenya kũthyũmũa na kwĩtaanĩthya.
eng: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

kam: Utee wa ukanga, kundu kwi syindu sya kusisya na kambi ni siendawa muno ni atalii.
eng: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

kam: Ethĩwa kĩeleelo kya mundu kuthi vandu ni kwenda umanya maundu mavo ma tene na syithio syoo muthemba uyu wa utalii witawa utalii wa syithio.
eng: If the objective of one's visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

kam: Atalĩĩ matembea kũndũ kĩvathũkany'o nthĩ kana omakasakũa kũtembea vandũ vamwe.
eng: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

kam: Asungũ ala masũmbikite nthi ino moona ũu ni meetisye ũtethyo.
eng: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

kam: ĩkũndĩ nĩ sya lasĩmĩthasya mwĩ nya ya mbee yĩovo 1st na 3rd New Hampshĩre regĩments ya aũme 200, nthĩ wa kolonel John stark na James Reed (ala ĩtĩma nĩmatwĩkĩe generals).
eng: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

kam: Aume ma Stark meevithite wiioni mwiso wa ngaliko ya yiulu ya vala akoloni mai.
eng: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

kam: Yĩla low tide mavingũie mwanya ũtee wa ũsĩ wa Mystic, ngalĩko ya ĩũlĩ wa umĩloni wa syũa wa Peninsula, mongeleelie wiio kwa mĩtũkĩ na ũkũta mũkuvĩ wa ĩvia ngalĩkonĩ ya ĩũlũ wathelela mũthianĩ wa kĩw'ũ kaũteenĩ kanini ka ũsĩ.
eng: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

kam: Gridley kana Stark aiie kilungu vakuvi vuti iana yimwe (mita miongo itatu) mbee wa wiio na anengane watho kana o na uu ndakaathe mbika ma kawaita mamivitukithye.
eng: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

kam: Vulani ya Amerika yeekwety'e kwambiisya mavithukii kuma ngali itatu syi kivathukany'o.
eng: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

kam: Munene John Cadwalder ai ambiisya mbithũkio ya ita sya Britain ula wi Bordentown ni kenda maikaetewe ũtethyo.
eng: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

kam: Munene wa jeshi James Ewing atwaa asikali ma jeshi maana muonza muingo wa ũsi kũu Trenton Ferry, akoosa kiao kya Assumnpink Creek na kusiia mumaitha wonthe ndakasembe.
eng: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

kam: Nguthu ila nene ya vinya wa aũme 2.400 yakĩlaa usi maili kenda ngaliko ya iulu ya Trenton, na ikaana nguthu ili, kimwe uungu wa Greene na kingi uungu wa Sullivan, ni kana maambiisye ukuna kau wa mbee wa kwakya.
eng: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

kam: Nũndũ wa ũalyũko kuma ĩsemba ya kwota kũthi ya nusu ya maĩli, vata wa mĩtũkĩ yu ti munene mũno naw'o ũũmĩĩsyo ũtw'ĩkĩte wa vata vyũ.
eng: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

kam: Kilasi kya mbee kya miler nusu, mundume utonya usinda ndatika ili, ailwe ni kwithwa e na siviti nzeo, ateo kwi yumiisya kwaile ithwa kwivo saa syonthe sya muisyo.
eng: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

kam: Kũsemba vandũ vaasa ivinda ya mbevo na kũthi njimu ya kuseovya mwii wa iũlu ni nzi nzeo ya kwiseovya weteele ivinda ya kũsemba.
eng: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

kam: Kula nesa kuitumaa asembi ala anini masembe nesa kwi kwoka indi ni kuseo kwa uima woo wa mwii.
eng: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

kam: Kwikala na uima museo wi mbalanzi, kunywa kiw'u nesa, na kuelewa nesa maundu ma kwongeleela maundu ta asu kutumaa musembi ethwa e na mosungio maseo na ingi mayendeew'a ni ithau.
eng: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

kam: Kũsemba vandũ vakũvi ni ĩthaũ ya mbesa nini indĩ kwina maũndũ mate ma w'o ĩũlũ wa mĩio ila yiendekaa ithaũni yiĩ.
eng: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

kam: Syindu no siuwe o undu ikwendeka, indi mbingi syasyo syithiawa na utethyo munini kana vathei iulu wa matokeo.
eng: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

kam: Asembi no mew'e mendeew'a ni kindu onakethwa syiina utethyo mwianiu kwoo.
eng: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

kam: Atom noyoswe ta ĩmwe kwa mavia me vata mũno ma kwaka syĩndũ syonthe.
eng: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

kam: Nĩkĩndũ kĩ vĩnya kũkwatya na kĩthaa na, kwĩanana na Bohr model, nĩũkĩlĩa sya katĩ syĩthaa ĩthyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ tũlũngũ tũnĩnĩ twitawa elekĩtronĩ, ota ũndũ planetĩ ĩthĩũkaa sũa - sĩsya ĩvĩsa ya 1.1.
eng: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

kam: Nucleus yĩthĩawa na ilungu ilĩ - neurons na protons.
eng: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

kam: Vulotoni syithiawa na uvano wa kwongela wa mwaki wa sitima, indi nasyo niutuloni siyithiawa na mwaki ona vanini. Elekituloni nasyo syithiawa na uvano wa kuola wa mwaki wa sitima.
eng: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

kam: Nĩ kenda kũsĩsya mũwaũ, nĩ lasĩma wambe kũsĩsya vala vekĩkĩe kĩko kyũ nĩ kenda wĩthwe wĩmũsũvĩĩkũ.
eng: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

kam: Ni wailitwe kumanya muungamo wa muumiw'a withi vakuvi nake na syonekany'o ila syukaa o mana.
eng: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

kam: Ila uumia uitata kutetheesya, no ukite kwananga maundu vyu.
eng: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

kam: Ukunikili ũu weethiie kuthĩnĩka ngoo mũno, wia na kwona thina ni syithiawa ivinda ya woo na kwonza kwa mũongo wa nthi.
eng: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

kam: No mauito ma mathina, ti kukw'a ngoo na wia waí kauta kila kyumwa nundu wa mavinda ma PA.
eng: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

kam: Ala me isesoni yimwe meendaa ukwatwa mbau kwa mwonekano muthuku wa woo uivathukany'a ivathukany'o sya woo utathelaa na kwiw'a utemwianie nundu wa kutinda uendete.
eng: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

kam: Woni, kana utonyi wa kwona itengemeaa na mutalatala wa mamutha ma kumanya kana metho.
eng: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

kam: Ve mithemba mingi ya mumbo wa metho, kivathukany'o kiyongeleka kwianana na mawendi ma I kyumbe.
eng: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

kam: Kuseuvw'a na miundo yi kivathukanio syithiawa na mautonyi me kivathukany'o, syithiawa na nivindukaa mituki kwianana na uvinduku wa makumbo na syithiawa na levoo syi kivathukany'o sya usungio, o ingi nisyendaa nzia syi kivathukany'o ni kana sielewe ni kila i kwikiwa na namba syi kivathukany'o ithukume nesa.
eng: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

kam: Utalo ni muvulany'o wa syindu sya kivathukany'o nthini wa kisio vulani.
eng: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

kam: Ila andu oonthe mavyanene me kwa populeshoni vamwe na tavia syoo metawa monomorphic.
eng: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

kam: Ila andũ moonania mithemba kauta ya tavia na methaa masensye maketha na tavia mbingi.
eng: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

kam: Mithwa íatianíaa na itua kundu kivathukany'o.
eng: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

kam: Ivinda yasyo ya kutembea, nguku itembea kwatuka na iithyumua ivinda ya muthenya.
eng: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

kam: Mũkolonĩ ambĩa mwendo wa aĩthĩ leũ wambĩa kũthela.ĩvĩndanĩ yĩĩ, mũkolonĩ nĩwaseũvasya tũsũmba tũla twa vĩndũawa kĩla mũthenya.
eng: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

kam: Kila imwe ya savali kana maseso aya ikuaa ilungu ya mithenya ta ikumi na muonza.
eng: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

kam: seli ni kyau? Ndeto seli yumanite na ndeto ya Kilatini "sela", ila imaanisyaa "kasumba kanini", na ndeto ino yakwataniw'e vamwe ni mutumii wa nduluvini aisisya undu kikuniko kya suva kiseuvitwe.
eng: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

kam: Seli niyo uniti ya syindu syonthe syi thau, na syindu syonthe syithwaa iseuvitw'e ni imwe kana seli mbingi.
eng: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

kam: Seli syithwaa syi laisi na maana ila uusoma yiulu wa maisa, ona syitawa "mavia ala makite maisa".
eng: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

kam: Nervous system niyo itumaa imbasi kwa naavu mwiini w'on the nikenda nthakame yikale itembeete mwiini na ite usumbuwa.
eng: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

kam: Ũmanyĩthani ũũ wa naavu noũtũmwe mĩtĩkĩ mũno mwĩĩnĩ w'onthe ĩla ĩtethasya kwiia mwĩĩ vate mbanga ya kũtelemw'a nĩ kĩndũ kyonthe.
eng: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

kam: ĩuutani ii syithiwa kisio kinini kute ĩuutani ila ingi syi vinya, ingi no syanange syindu ila syi nziani ya syo.
eng: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

kam: Syĩuutani ni syikuua miti, ikaumwa ivwaũ nyumbani na ikaukilywa ngali kiseveni. Syiũutani ila nthũkũ vyũ syikalaa masaa atatũ.
eng: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

kam: Ilingi ii nene syina kiseve kya nginya 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).
eng: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

kam: Andu methiitwe maiseuvya na kutumia ioo sya unenevya syindu kwa ivinda ya makili na makili ma myaka.
eng: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

kam: Indi, telescope ya w'o ya mbee yaseovĩwe kũya Europe ivinda ya myakani ya 1600 ikilye kuthela.
eng: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

kam: Ndũlũvenĩ ino syatumiaa lenzi ili kuthikithya syindu syi kuasa syikale ta syi vakuvi na nene.
eng: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

kam: Itomo na utoonu kukethaa na itu na ni mituo ya ngwatanio ila aingi matetheka, kukethaa syindu mbingi sya kukwata na nthini wa ivinda inini mena utoonu.
eng: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

kam: Ni wikwatyo andu mamanye kana wendi woo munene ni kuthukumana na andu angi me vamwe.
eng: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

kam: Andũ aĩngĩ mendaa mũthenya andũ makathĩ ndatanĩ ĩngĩ na kũmanya nthĩ ĩngĩ, andũ amwe maseng'aa nĩkyaũ kĩkũ na amwe maĩkĩĩa alĩens kana thayũ ĩngĩ nosyĩkale ndatanĩ ĩngĩ.
eng: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

kam: Ateo, kethwa ũũ nũkwĩkĩka no ithwa ite ĩvĩnda yĩasa. Ndata syĩthaa itaanĩe na vaasa mũno na maili trĩlĩonĩ katĩ wa ndata ĩla nĩ "mũtũĩ".
eng: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

kam: Noethwa muthenya umwe, nzukuku syaku ikethwa siungye iulu wa nthi ya syindu nzaanu syiisenga iulu wa ancestors moo ma tene?
eng: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

kam: nyamũ ĩseũvĩtwe n cells mbĩngĩ.syĩĩsa syĩndũ na sĩyĩthĩa nthĩnĩ wa syo.nyamũ mbĩngĩ no ĩtembee.
eng: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

kam: Nyamu syoka nisyo syi iliko (ateo ti nyamu syonthe; ikuyu, kwa ngelekany'o, iyingwa kiliko).
eng: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

kam: Nyamu syonekaa kila vandu iulu wanthi. Syinzaa ku nthi, ikathambia ku maukangani, na ikauluka kuu matuni.
eng: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

kam: Cell' ni kalembeta kala kanini vyu ka vata mwiini wa kindu ki thayu.
eng: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

kam: Seli yumanite na ndeto ya Latin cella ila iminiaa kalumu kanini.
eng: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

kam: Wasyaisya syindu syi thayu nthi wa kaindo ka unenevy'a syindu ukoona kana iseuvitw'e na ithyululu kana tulungu tuini.
eng: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

kam: Robert Hooke, mundu wa mbailongyi kuma uungelesa, niwoonie tuindo tunini twianene ngali syonthe ngunikoni aitumia kindu kya utethesya kwona tuindo tunini.
eng: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

kam: Syailyi ta lumu. Nĩwe waĩ mundu wa mbee kwona seli ngwũ.
eng: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

kam: Elements na compounds no syume kuma kwa muthemba umwe kuthi uungi vate kusenzya.
eng: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

kam: Nitrogen ta ngasi mbato yio syindu o imwe ta Nitrogen sya muvai wa kiw'u. Muvai wa kiw'u undu withwaa uilye ni muvuthu ateo molecules syithwaa syi undumwe.
eng: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

kam: Kiwu ni ngelekany'o ingi. Kiwu kyonthe kiseuvitw'e ni twindu twa aindrongen na atomu imwe ya nzeve yo veva na nthini.
eng: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

kam: yithiawa na umbo umwe wa nthini yithw'e ni nzeve, kiw'u, kana ivia.
eng: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

kam: O na kwithw'a mumbo wayo ula twonaa no uvinduke, umbo wa kemikoo nduvindukaa.
eng: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

kam: Mavinda ni kindu kithiawa kila vandu tui, na kikwataa syindu syonthe ila twikaa, indu ni kyumu kueleeka.
eng: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

kam: Ivinda ni isometwe ni asomi ma ndini, ui, na saenzi myaka makili maingi.
eng: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

kam: Ivinda ni tuyikusiiya ta ilingu sya maundu makethiwa mithenya yukite, kuvitia kwa mithenya ila tui ooyu muvaka mithenya mivitu.
eng: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

kam: Ivinda onayo no nzia tutumiia kusyaanisya (uasa) wa maundu meethiwa.
eng: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

kam: No umake kuvita kwa ivinda we mweene na kuisya kwisyokeleela kwa ivinda ya kithyululu ivinda ua kithyululu ni kindu kikikaa ingi na ingi.
eng: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

kam: Matuku aa kompyuta itumiawa kuvindua visa na vindio.
eng: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

kam: Visa sya kwĩloela sya vata mũno no siseuvĩw'e kombyũtanĩ, na mũthemba ũũ wa ũseũvya visa nĩwongelekete ũtũmĩwa televiseninĩ na vitiunĩ.
eng: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

kam: Mavinda maingi wathi useuvaw'a na kompyuta ngomau kwa kuseuvya na kuvulany'a mawasya.
eng: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

kam: Kwa kilungu kiasa myakani ya 1900 na ya 2000, nikwaikiiite jana andu ma mbee kwikala New Zealand ni Maoiri ala asyimaa masuni manene metawa moas.
eng: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

kam: Ngewa ila yaasya kana yisilya ya andu ma Maori mathamie kuma Polynesia kwa nzia nene na moosa New Zealand kuma Moriori na mambiia uimi wa ngwatanio ya njamii.
eng: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

kam: Uu wiovo, ukusi mweu wionany'a kana Moriori mai nguluvu nene ya Maori ala mathamie kuma New Zealand kuthi ithimani sya Chatham, maseuvitye kithio kyoo kikivathukany'o na ki muuo.
eng: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

kam: Kwai mbai ingi ithamani ii sya Chathamyitawa Maori ila yaumite New Zealand.
eng: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

kam: Meeyitie Moriori kwai makau o kauta na mwisowe, muvai wa Moriori wavetangwa vyu.
eng: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

kam: Andu ala makonanitw'e kwa myaka kauta matutetheeisye na kumanya mavinya na wendi witu o vamwe na kuasesi mawetu na mauvaluku maitu.
eng: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

kam: Yila twethukiisye andu mainengane ngewa syoo ene, sya misyi yoo, na sya mawiani moo, ni twakwatie mwanya wa ukunikila kwa unthini mithenya mivituku na andu amwe ala makiitie kwa useo kana uthuku syithio sya I kambuni.
eng: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

kam: O ila uelewa ni umo wa mundu manya ti undu umwe na kumanya kithio kyake, nitumaa mundu amanya vala ui kwa umo wa mundu wa kambuni.
eng: While understanding one's history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

kam: Nthini wa kuthima mauseo na kuendeea na kumanya mauvaliku, andu na ala methiawa vau oonthe nimamanyaa o kwa uito myolooto, wia na syindu ila isukumaa kampuni.
eng: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

kam: Ivindani yii, tuililikana maita kauta mavitu ma tavia ya uviasala na maendeeo mayo ni mateetheisye andu kwitikilana na mitalatala myeu na nzia nzau ya ikanisa yaku.
eng: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

kam: Ngewa imwe ta isu sya maendeeo nisyaolile mawia ma kusenzya, o ila ingi syaendee kusenzya ivinda yukite.
eng: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

kam: Kusuania kuvyanene nikuminaa mathina ala makwatanasya mesilya kivathukany'o nikenda ukwate usungio.
eng: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

kam: Woni wa ĩsũanĩa ta yĩĩ nĩ mĩtũkĩ, kĩlĩĩko na ũseo vyũ, o na kwona ũw'o, kũtũmĩa nthĩa ila syĩkw'o, kwosanya maũvoo.
eng: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

kam: Kindũ kya vata vyũ yisilyani yii ni: Ve ũsũngio umwe wa w'o. Wiisililya mausungio eli, uw'o kana ũvungũ.
eng: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

kam: Kusoania kwa nzia iĩ nikuthanĩtwe na saenzi na nzĩa ingĩ sya kawaita.
eng: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

kam: Andu masuaniaa uu methwaa me sawa, methwaa matonya ulilikana patani, kumina mathina na kuthukuma kwa mitiani ya maundu ma saenzi.
eng: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

kam: Andu nĩmo mena kĩnengo kya mwanya kya kũsoma akili sya iingi.
eng: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

kam: Kiu ni kwonany'a kana twina utonyi wa kumanya undu andu mekwona, mavangite kwika, kuaikiia, kumanya kana kwendeew'a.
eng: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

kam: Kati wa mautonyi aa, kuelewa wendi wa andu angi ni kindu ki vata. Itumaa twithwa tutonya kumina syindu syivinya sya maundu ma kwika.
eng: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

kam: Kwa mũvyano, ũkona mũndũ ndatũla ndĩlĩsya ya ngalĩ, wasya akwete kuya ngalĩ yeene.
eng: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger's car.

kam: Nukwenda usilĩlwa kĩvathũkany'o ketha niwaaisye mbungũo sya ngalĩ yake na nĩyo watataa kũvũnzya alike.
eng: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

kam: MRI yina mũsingĩ wa Fisikisi witawa nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), ula wamanyikanie myakani ya 1930 ni Felix Bloch (aithukuma yunivasiti ya Stanford) na Edward Purcell (kuma yunivasiti ya Harvard).
eng: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

kam: Nthini wa chanelini kiu, makumbo ma sivaki na ma redio matumaa atumu syambiisya kumya singinoo sya letio.
eng: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

kam: Mwaka wa 1970, Raymond Damadian, ndakitali wa uiiti, na musomi wa saenzi, ni wa vumbuie mwambiliilyo wa kutumie mashini ya kukuna visa ta muio wa kuthima nthini wa uiiti.
eng: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

kam: Mwaka ina itina niw'o valua wanenganiwe, ula niw'o wai wambee nthi yonthe kunenganwe muveani wa MRI.
eng: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

kam: Mwakanĩ wa 1977, dakitalĩ Damadian nĩwamĩnĩebkũseũvya MRI skana ya mbee ya mwĩĩ wonthe ĩla wa mĩtĩe "indomitable"
eng: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first "whole-body" MRI scanner, which he called the "Indomitable".

kam: Uneeni ũla wa kũmanĩsya nũnenganaa mũndũ mwanya wa kwĩsilya na ĩndĩ kwĩka.
eng: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

kam: Ni inengaa amanyiwa utonyi wa kuthukuma undu matonya na undu miao ikumavikia.
eng: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

kam: Onaĩngĩ, vemasaa manini ma kũkũna wĩa ũtemũtalĩle masaa. (bremer, 1998)
eng: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

kam: Ũtũmĩĩ wa mitandao ũnenga asomĩ mwanya wa kũkwata kĩsomo mavĩnda onthe.
eng: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

kam: Asomi no manengane maukulyo kwi aalimu ivinda o yonthe kwi muthenya na sikeeteela usungio wa mituki, vandu va kweteela mbika ivinda yingi ya kwonana uthyu-kwa-uthyu.
eng: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

kam: Nzĩa ya kũsoma ya matũkũ aa nĩnenganaa mwanya wa kũelewa kũma mĩtũo ya tene. Vaĩ nzĩa ĩmwe nzeo ya kũsoma.
eng: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

kam: Ũw'o, vaiĩ kĩndũ kĩseo o na kĩmwe kya kusoma. Kũsoma kwĩthĩawa nthini wa ũtuika na katĩ katĩ wa mũmanyiw'a na umanyi ula ũkunengwa.
eng: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

kam: Maũndũ ala twonete ma mĩtũkĩ monthe ma ĩka-we-mwene na ũvĩtũkya wa ũvoo, shoo sya televiseni ila syambatene na kwĩmanyĩthya syonany'a ũndũ ũũ.
eng: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

kam: Aingĩ maitũ twĩthĩaa twĩloele ilungu televiseninĩ ila itatũtavasya ĩũlũ wa nzĩa kana kĩndũ kĩĩsĩle kĩla tũtakeesa ũkwatanĩa nakyo kana kũtũmĩa ũmanyi ũsu.
eng: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

kam: Tuikaseovithya ngali yitu ĩngĩ, kwaka nthongo nza wa nyumba kwĩtũ, kũthĩ Perũ kũsĩsya myako ya ĩvĩnda ya tene, kana kũseũvya ĩngĩ nyũmba ya mũtũĩ wĩtũ.
eng: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

kam: Nimuvea kwa waya ula wisile ukangani ukakwatany'a Yulovu na setilaiti, Greenland yu nikwatanitw'e nesa yina kilungu kya 93 yiulu wa yiana mena Intaneti.
eng: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

kam: Oteli kana ala mauthoketye (kethwa wiikala kwa nyumba ya uthokw'a kana yaku mweene) ni muno kwithwa na wifi kana kombyuta ikwatanitw'e na indaneti, na mautuo oonthe mena mukaawa wina indaneti kana kundu kungi kwa wanda kwina wifi.
eng: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

kam: O ta undũ vawetetwe vau ulu, ona vala ndeto "Eskimo" yithaa yitikilitwe United States ni yosawa ta isitwa ithuku ni andu mate ma United States Mũno mũno ma Canada.
eng: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

kam: Na withwe uyiw'a ndeto itumiawa ni ekali ma Greenlandic, andu ma kuma nza nimaila eka umitumia.
eng: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

kam: Eene ma Greenland meyĩtaa Inuit me kananda na Kalaalleq (kwa wingĩ), Greenlander, kũu Greenland.
eng: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

kam: Meko ma ũng'endilĩ, na mawendĩ mathũkũ kũla kwĩ aenĩ ndĩsĩkanĩwe kũũ Greenland. Ona kũũ mĩsyĩnĩ kũyĩthaa na "kũndũ kũthũkũ".
eng: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

kam: Mbevo itonya kwithiwa no my'o muisyo munene utonya ukomana na mundu ula uteyumbanitye.
eng: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

kam: Watembea Greenland ivindani ya mbevo (uililikana kana o undu uthi Iulu, now'o kukwithiwa kuthithu), ni undu wa vata kuka na ngua sya muutia mbianu.
eng: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

kam: Mĩthenya mĩasa ya ĩvinda ya sua noyĩete mathĩna ta kũkwata too mwĩanũ na mathĩna mamwĩĩ makũnanĩtwe na kũkosa too.
eng: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

kam: Ivindani ya syua, ithwa wi metho o na tumuu twa Nordic. O na kau tuyietae uwau wonthe, no tuthatye muno.
eng: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

kam: O ila ekonomi ya Francisco ukonanaw'a na kwendeesya atalii ma kilasi kya nthi yonthe, ekonomi yayo ni inyaiiku.
eng: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

kam: Uandĩkanĩ ũla mũnene wĩthĩa maũndũ ala ma andũ mesĩ wĩa, selikalĩnĩ, mbesanĩ, ũtandĩthya, na ũtaliinĩ.
eng: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

kam: Wonany'o uu wa kauta wathini, sinemani, literature na kithio kitumiawa muno kutetheetye misyi minene kumanyika nthi yonthe.
eng: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

kam: San Francisco ninenevetye muvea wa utalii na maoteli, mikaawa, na kundu kwo komania kukali.
eng: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

kam: San Francisco no yo imwe ya kundu kuseo vyu nthini isu nundu wa maliu angi ma Asia: ma Korea, Thai, India, na Japan.
eng: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

kam: kũtembea kuthi Walt Disney kwonanasya kyalo kya vandũ vatheũ nthĩnĩ wa mĩsyĩ mĩngĩ Amelika.
eng: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

kam: Kutembea "kúla kúmwe" kwithwaa vamwe na kuuluka na ndeke kuthi kiwanzani kinene kya ndeke kya Orlando, ukakwatany'a na oteli wa Disney ula withwaa vau, ukekala vau kyumwa kimwe na uisyoka musyi.
eng: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

kam: Ve ivathukany'o itekithimo itonya ithwa syivo, ateo uu utwikaa kana niw'o andu aingi maminiaa ila mekuneenea yiulu wa "kuthi Disney World".
eng: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

kam: Tikiti mbingi ithoetw'e kwisila indanetini sya athoosya ta eBay kana Craiglist syithiawa tikiti sya mithenya mingi sya utwila kuna vandu vamwe kuthi vangi.
eng: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

kam: Onakaũ ũũ nũndũ wa kĩla ĩvĩnda nĩ mũvatane nĩ dĩsney. Tĩkĩtĩ syasyo ĩkũĩaw'a.
eng: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

kam: Kwĩkala kambĩnĩ nthĩ wa Grand Canyon kwendaa valũa wa nthĩ ya ĩtina.
eng: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

kam: Valua ni nini ila syiusuvia canyon, na syithwaa ikwatikana muthenya wa mbee wa mwei, myei ina mbee wa mwei wa kuambiia.
eng: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

kam: Kwooũ, lũũsa wa kũsyoka nthĩ kwambĩĩa matũkũ ona meva noyĩthe yĩkwatĩkana kwambĩĩa 1 mwai wa mbee.
eng: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

kam: Myanya ya kũndũ kwisikie mũno ta Bright Angel Campground ila ivakene na Phantom Ranch ni yusuua mthenya wa mbee andũ maambia kuivia myanya.
eng: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

kam: Ve mavalua manini matiele maiitwe kwa ala ma kuthi ma mauu na kwa ala meuka ma mbee, kwa nzia ya ula wavika wa mbee niwe ukunengwa.
eng: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

kam: Kulika Avilika ya itheo na ngali ni nzia nzeo ya kwona wanake wa kisio kyu na kuvika kula kwi nzia sya ndambuka kula atalii matavika muno.
eng: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

kam: Undu uu nowikwe kwa ngali ya kawaita uvangite nesa ateo 4x4 vendaa na kundu kwingi kuendeka na ndia nthanthau sya 4x4.
eng: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

kam: Ikia kilikoni kana kuvanga ateo Avilika ya itheoni ni ndumu na nthi ila mutui ti ndumu.
eng: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

kam: Syĩndũ ila syendekanaa nĩ kaa mũndũ anewe mathangũ ma ũlika nthĩ ĩngĩ na mbesa sya'ũmaĩvĩa syĩthĩawa kĩvathũkanyo kwĩanana na nthĩ ĩla ĩkũĩnengane na kwĩanana na nthĩ ĩla uumĩte.
eng: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

kam: Kĩla nthĩ nĩyĩthaa na mĩao yayo mbene ĩla yĩwetete nĩkyaũ kyaĩle kwĩtha ngalĩnĩ kya mĩtũkĩ.
eng: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

kam: Tauni ya Victoria Falls ngaliko ya westani ilembetani ya Zimbabwe kukilanilya muvaka kuma Livingstone, Zambia, na vakuvi na Botswana.
eng: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

kam: Soko usu wi vakuvi na muvaluko usu wa kiw'u, na ni ukusyo munene, indi kikusyo kii kya atalii kinenganae myanya mingi kwa andu ala mekwenda kusisya vamwe na ala meumantha syindu nzau.
eng: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

kam: Ivindani ya mbua (mwei wa ikumi na umwe nginya wakatatu) kiwu kiithwa ki kingi na ndulumo syiithwa syi sya kwendeesya.
eng: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

kam: Wi muikithye kuthitha wakilanilya kiao kana watembea utee wa kula kiwu kiiyikya.
eng: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

kam: Ona oou, ni kwoondũ ndwiona nesa kula kiwũ kĩkwĩnyĩkya nũndũ ni kĩngi.
eng: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

kam: Kavuli ka Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 no itonye ithwa noko kavuli ke nguma kiimani kiu, sini ya kumanya ya Howard ya 1922 ya Cartel ya mathiko mavange nesa ma.
eng: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

kam: Walingany'a na tũvũlĩ twa ndongoĩ sya ũsũmbĩ, o na kaũ, kavũlĩ ka Tũtankhamũn vaĩ aja ya kũkatembelea, nũndũ nĩ kanĩĩnĩ na tĩ kanake ta tũvũlĩ tũla tũngĩ.
eng: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

kam: Ula ukwenda kwona undu kimba kii kyanangitwe ila andu meenda kukiumya isandukuni ndeona nundu no mutwe na ituo syonekee.
eng: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

kam: Mothwii asu manee ma kavuli kau maivo ingi, indi nimavetetwe makatwawa isumbani ya kusuvia syindu sya tene ku misili.
eng: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

kam: Aeni mena ivinda inini nimo methwa me vaseo kutumia ivinda yoo me vandu vangi.
eng: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

kam: Phnom Krom ila yi kilomita 12 ngaliko ya itheo ya umilo wa sua ya Siem Reap. Ikalu yii yi iulu wa kiima yaakiwe mwiso wa myaka ya 900 ivinda ya Musumbi Yasovarman.
eng: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

kam: Nzeve ii ya kimako ya ikalu na kwona iulu wa iia ya Tonle Sap nitumaa kulisa kiima kwithwa kwi na useo wakw'o.
eng: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

kam: Kũtembea kuthi vandu vau nokũkwatanĩw'e nesa vyũ na kyalo kya ĩtalũ kya kũthi ĩianĩ.
eng: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

kam: Pass ya Angkor niyendekaa nikenda ulike ikaluni kwoou ndukolwe ni kuka na pasipoti yaku ila uelekele Tonle Sap.
eng: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

kam: Yerusalemu niw'o musyi munene wa Isilaeli, o na kau nthi ingi mbingi na Ngwatanio ya Nthi ndimy'osaa taw'o musyi munene wa Isilaeli.
eng: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

kam: Musyi munene wa tene kuu iĩmani sya Judea withwa na istoli yi muyo ikwete kuma myaka makili mithelu.
eng: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

kam: Musyi usu munene ni muthesye nundu wa ndni ila sya uthaitha Ngai umwe - Ya Ayuti, Kikilisito na Kiisilamu, na ithiaa ta kati kati ya maundu ma ki veva, ndini, na syithio.
eng: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

kam: Nũndũ wa ũ vata wa kĩ ndĩni wa mũsyĩ ũsu mũnene, na mũno mũno kũndũ kwingĩ kwa kwĩloela nthĩnĩ wa ngalĩko ngũũ ya mũsyĩ ũsu, Yelũsalemu nĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa kũndũ kwa kwendwa nĩ atalii Ĩsilaeli.
eng: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

kam: Yelusaleme yi kundu kwingi kwa isitolia, kwa kwinza na kwa kithio, vamwe na isese sya utandithya ithengeanie vamwe na sya kwendeesya, kundu kwa kuiia, na kundu kwa kwitanithya.
eng: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

kam: Ecuador yienda eene nthi ma Cuba matumiwe valua mbee wa matanalika Ecuador kwisila iwanza sya ndeke sya nthi yonthe kana kwitikilithwa kwa voindi.
eng: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

kam: Valua uu niwaile kwitikilw'a ni muvea ma maundu manza ma Ecuador, na uyiatiia miao kauta.
eng: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

kam: Maundu aa methwaa maseuvitw'e ni kenda withie kuthama ni laisi kati ka nthi syeli.
eng: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

kam: Eene nthi ma Cuba ala mena kaati sya ngilini maile uthokea uvisi wa Ecuador nikenda mavetangwe kwa iseeso yii.
eng: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

kam: Pasipoti yitu no nginya yithwe yi mbitikilithye kwa mwei thanthatu kuvika matuku maku ma kutembea. Ndambuka ya kuthi na mbee niyendekaa kwonany'a ivinda ila ukwikala undu yiasavite.
eng: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

kam: Savali sya andũ aingi ni mbesa nini, kwooũ ketha wi weka kana wina mũnyanyaũ, tata ũmanthe andũ angi mũseovye kikũndi kya andũ ana kana thanthatũ ni kenda mũive mbesa nini.
eng: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

kam: O va ilye uu, undu ndwaile ema ukuthiny'a, nundu mavinda maingi atalii nimakuanaw'a nikenda maususye ngali.
eng: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

kam: yĩĩlye mũno ta nzĩa ya kũkenga andũ kũĩkĩĩa kana maĩlũ kũĩva mũnango.
eng: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

kam: Yi kuu matuni ngali ya yiuluni ya Machu Picchu ni kiima kii kivauuku muno, kaingi kyumilaa visani sya matialy'o asu.
eng: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

kam: Ĩilye ta yaũkĩsya kuma vau nthĩ, na nĩ mwambato mũũngamu na mũmũ mũno, ĩndĩ andũ ala me mĩĩ ĩtaĩ mathĩna no matonye ũlĩsa nthĩnĩ wa ndatĩka ta 45.
eng: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

kam: Sĩtevu sya mavia niseũvĩtw'e vakũvĩ kĩla kasĩlanĩ, na kũla kũtheeũ kwĩna kũndũ kwa kwĩkwatĩla kũseũvĩtw'e na waya wa kyũma.
eng: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

kam: Usu wi o vo, eteela kuemwa ni kuveva, isuvie isio syi itheeo muno muno ila syina kimeu nundu no kwithwe na muisyo mituki.
eng: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

kam: Ve ngunga nini vakuvĩ na ĩũlũ ĩla no mbika yĩsĩlwe katĩ katĩ wamy'o, yĩ nthĩ mũno na ya ũvivilwa vyũ.
eng: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

kam: Kwona kundu na nyamu sya kithekani sya Galapagos kwikawa nesa italuni, o ta undu Charles Darwin wekie mwakani wa 1835.
eng: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

kam: Masiwa mavitite 60 nimesilaa nzia ya kiwuni ya Galapagos ila yi unene wa kuma akua 8 nginya 100.
eng: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

kam: andu aingi mayivaa uthei woo tene tene matuko matanamba uvika (nundu masiwa methaa mausuite ivinda ya mbesa).
eng: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

kam: Sisya kana muungamii ula ukuiva kwisila kwake ni mundu ueleetwe na kusomea maundu ma Galapagos wina umanyi museo wa meli syi kivathukany'o.
eng: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

kam: Ũu wikiithya kana wendi waku fulani na/kana unyivu niweananithw'a na isiwa ila yimaile.
eng: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

kam: Mbee ya Spanish mavike twi sengyali ya 16, ngaliko ya iulu ya Chile yai ungu wa utongoi wa Inca o ila eene nthi ma Araucanian (Mapuche) matuie kati kati na ngaliko ya iulu ya Chile.
eng: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

kam: Mapũche maĩ amwe katĩ wa ĩkũndĩ ĩla nĩnĩ sya Amelika syeyĩũngamĩe, ĩla syitalikitwe ũnenĩnĩ wa Spanish muvaka ila chĩle yakwatie wĩyathĩ.
eng: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

kam: Ona kutw'ika Chile yatangaasie kwisumbika mwaka wa 1810 katikati wa makau ma Napoleon ala matiie Spain itena silikali nene ikuthukuma myaka kauta, usindi wi kavaa iulu wa asungu ma Spain ndwaa ithiwa nginya 1818.
eng: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

kam: Republic ya Dominican (spanish: republica Dominicana) ni nthi ya caribbean ila yitiawa nusu umuloni wa sua na kithama kya hispaniola, kila kithiiwa vamwe na Haiti.
eng: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

kam: Eka o nthangathĩ ila syĩ ndee wa ũkanga na syiima, nthi isũ ni mũsyi wa ndua ila nguu muno vyu ya Europe nthini wa Amelicas, ila yu ni kilungu kimwi kya Domingo.
eng: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

kam: Kithama kyu kyambite ikalwa ni Tainos na Caribes. Namo Caribes mai andu maneenaa kithyomo kya Arawaka ala mavikite vandu 10,000 BCE.
eng: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

kam: Myaka minini itina wa akunikili kuma Europe kuvika, utalo wa andu ma Tainos ni woleketwe muno ni andu ma Spain ala mamakĩlilye vinya.
eng: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

kam: Kwianana na Fray Bartolome de las Casas (Tratado de las Indians) kati wa 1492 na 1498 ala mavivukiie Spanish mooaie andu ta 100,000 ma muvai wa Tainos.
eng: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

kam: Jardin de la Union. Yanya yii yaakiwe ta atrium ya wiw'ano wa sengyali ya 17, o vala Templo de San Diego niw'o mwako ula utiítwe.
eng: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

kam: Yũ nĩyo ĩtũmĩkaa ta mwako wa katĩ, na vethaa ve maũndũ maingĩ maendee vo, mũthenya na ũtũkũ.
eng: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

kam: Ve mikaawa mingi ithyuukite muunda usu, na muthenya na maiyoo nikwithiawa mathau ma mbathi na angi ta asu nthini wa vandu va uthumua vau nza.
eng: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

kam: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the kĩss). Mĩamba ĩlĩ ĩtĩlanĩtwe nĩ kĩthĩmo kya 69cm nĩw'o mũsyĩ mũkũũ wa wendo.
eng: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

kam: Umanengete o mbesa nini syana imwe siutavya I ngewa.
eng: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

kam: kĩthũkũma kya Bowen nĩvaendawa mũno kwa syalo sya mũthenya kana wĩkendĩ nũndũ nĩkwĩthaa kũtwaa masĩwa, kũtembea, ndũka, kũndũ kwa kũthũmũa na ĩngĩ mbĩngĩ.
eng: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

kam: Njamii nzeo yi Howe Sound o wavita Vancouver, na no umikwate kwisila taxi sya kuvanga ila ukuma kithama kya Granville kuu nza wa taoni ya Vancouver.
eng: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

kam: Kwa ala mendete maseso ma nza no matembee o mbola ukangani uelekele kula kumililaa yayaya.
eng: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

kam: (Kũtwaa ngalĩ ĩsaa nyĩmwe na nũsũ kũma Vancouver) n kwa mbesa mbĩngĩ lakĩnĩ n vesĩkĩe nũndũ wa mathaũ ma mwaka wa 2010 ma ĩvĩndanĩ ya ũthĩthũ.
eng: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

kam: Siũũka ĩanĩ North America ivinda ya uthithũ na uilisa syima na isulũlũ ivinda ya sua.
eng: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

kam: Valua syailwe ni kulisaviwa tene. Wailwe ni kwithwa na valua ni kenda wikale wiyoo wonthe vaa Sirena.
eng: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

kam: Sirena nivo vandũ va asyĩmi voka vanenganae kũndũ kwa ũkoma na lĩu mũvyũ ĩũlũ wa kambĩ. La Leona, San Pedrillo, na Los Patos sinenganae o kambĩ vataĩ lĩu.
eng: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

kam: Ni vatonyeka ukakwata valua imwe kwa imwe kuma Ranger Station kuu Puerto Jimenez, ateo mayitikilaa kaati.
eng: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

kam: Wia wa kupark (MINAE) ndunenganae mwanya wa parking nthini wa ivinda yiasa ya mwei umwe mbeangeni ivinda ya kuvika.
eng: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

kam: CafeNet El Sol niyithwaa na kumbuku kwa tene na mbesa sya Amelika ndola 30, kana ndola ikumi kwa muthenya umwe; ve livoti mbeange ithanguni yoo.
eng: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

kam: Cook Island ni nthi yi kati kati wa kiw'u ina ngwatanio na New Zealand, yi nthini wa Polynesia, kati kati wa itheo ya Pacific ocean.
eng: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

kam: Ni archipelago vala ve ithama 15 syaanikite kuvita milioni 2.2 km2 mbaalini.
eng: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

kam: Syina ivinda yimwe ya masaa ta Hawaii, nthi isu syi kati kati wa kiw'u mavinda angi isuaniawa ta "Hawaii nthi y'uungu".
eng: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

kam: Ateo nĩ nini, ililikanasya atalii amwe akũũ kuma Hawaii mbeangenĩ wa nthĩ vate mĩkaawa mĩnene ya atalii na maendeeo angĩ.
eng: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

kam: Ithama sya Cook iyingwa mĩsyĩ mĩnene ateo syĩna ithama 15 kĩvathũkany'o. ĩla nene nĩ Rarotonga na Aitutaki.
eng: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

kam: Kwa nthĩ ila syendee nesa ũmũnthĩ, kuseuvya kitanda kya deluxe na lĩũ wa kwakya kũtwĩkĩthĩtw'e muthemba wa ati.
eng: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

kam: Mwiso muthyani, B&Bs isindanaa nundu wa syindu ili: kukomani na mbrekifasti.
eng: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

kam: O kwou, twi vandu vaseo uu mundu niwaile umantha syindu sya itanda ila sya mbesa mbingi, vatonyeka ivula ya utuma na moko kana kitanda kya tene.
eng: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

kam: Kyauya kya kwakya no kithiwe na maliu ma ivindani ma vandu vau kana liu uuitwe nesa ni ula ukethetw'e.
eng: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

kam: Mwako ũu no ta wa nyũmba ngũu yiseovetwe ya nzia sya tene, nthi ni iseovetwe na yina vandũ va kũthambia.
eng: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

kam: kũlĩka ngalĩnĩ yakũ na kũthĩ kyalonĩ kĩasa kũnengaa mwĩndũ mwĩw'ĩle mũseo.
eng: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

kam: Kivathukany'o na ngali nene, niikwatya niwisene na undu wailitwe ni kutwaa ngali yaku nini na niwisi unyivu wayo.
eng: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

kam: Kwaka maeema malini ya mweene kana tauni ya saisi o na wiva nokutume andu malyaiilya kindu kite maana.
eng: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

kam: Kwa ũkuvĩ, kũtũmĩa ngalĩ yaku nĩ nthĩa nzeo mũno ya kũthi ndembea sya lelũnĩ ĩndĩ kaingĩ ti nthĩa ya kũthi ũthũmũo wa kambinĩ.
eng: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

kam: Kũtũa ũtũmĩĩte ngalĩ nĩkũtonyeka ketha wĩna ngalĩ nene, Sedan kana Station Wagon yĩna ĩvĩla syĩtonya kũkomwa.
eng: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

kam: Mikaawa imwe yithiawa na kindu yosete kuma golden age ya nzia sya ngali sya mwaki na mivia ya ukanga; mbee wa kau wa keli wa nthi yonthe, myakani ya maana ikumi na kenda kana mwambililyoni wa miongo ili.
eng: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

kam: Maoteli aa mai vala athui na ala mai nguma ma umunthi methwa mekalaa, na maina liu wa wioo museo na maisa ma wioo maseo.
eng: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

kam: Syinduũ sya tene, kuema itha na syindũ sya mithenya ino na kũkua nikukonanwa namo.
eng: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

kam: Ona vala ni ma andũ mbene, mala kauta asũmbĩ ma nthi ingĩ na anene angĩ ma nthi ingĩ nimekalaa kuũ mooka ndambũka.
eng: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

kam: Mutembei wina ilovia nesa no aamue kutembea nthi yonthe na ndeke, anoetw'e ni kwikala maotelini aa on the.
eng: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

kam: ikundi ya kukuany'a utethyo ni ngwatanio ila ikwatanasya atalii na andu maku misyi ila maendete kutembelea.
eng: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

kam: kũlĩka mũtandaonĩ ũsũ kwendaa ũsyũsye mathangũ mũtandaonĩ, anakaũ ve ĩngĩ yeenda kũĩkĩĩthwya.
eng: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

kam: List ya ala mauthokya yithwaa inenganitwe kwisila kwa kuprint na/kana kiseeveni, saa ingi nundu wa kwendekethw'a ni atembei ala angi.
eng: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

kam: Kwikala musyini wa mundu wa nthi ya ntha kwa thooa munini kwambiisw'e mwei wa mbee mwaka wa 2004 itina wa museuny'a wa syindu sya nthini sya kombyuta Casey Fenton ukwata ndeke ya kuivia kyalo kwa thooa wa nthi kuthi Iceland indi ndai na vandu va kwikala.
eng: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

kam: Atumiye amanyiwa imeili ma yunivasiti ya kisio na akwata namba mbingi sya andu meyumitye kumunenga vandu va kwikala mana.
eng: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

kam: Kundũ kũu kwa kũkoma kwithaa na andũ ma mũika - ta ma myaka ta mbao - indi no withie atalii akũuangu ku.
eng: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

kam: Vamĩlĩ syĩ syana ti mboneki mũno, ĩndĩ nyumba imwe sya ũkoma nĩmetĩkĩlasya tũsũmbanĩ twoo meoka.
eng: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

kam: Beijĩng mũsyĩ wa China nĩ vo vakethĩwa ve mathaũ ma Olympik ma ĩvĩnda ya mbevo mwakanĩ wa 2022, ala makaũtwĩkĩtha mũsyĩ wa mbee wa kwĩthĩwa wĩna mathaũ ma Olympik ma ĩvĩndanĩ ya sũa n ĩvindanĩ ya mbevo.
eng: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

kam: Beijing nĩyo ĩkũũngamĩa syathĩ sya kũvĩnga na kũvĩngũa na mathaũ ma nthĩnĩ wa nyũmba ma ĩa.
eng: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

kam: Mathau angi ma kusiuuka makeethwa kuu Taizicheng ngaliko ya usiuuka kuu Zhangjiakou, ta kilomita 220 (maili 140) kuma Mbeijini.
eng: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

kam: Makalũ maingĩ methwaa na mboka ya mwaka kwambĩĩya mwei wa ĩkũmĩ na ũmwe na ĩithela mwei wa katano katĩkatĩ, kĩla kĩsenzasya kwĩanana na kalenda ka mwaka ka kĩla ĩkalũ.
eng: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

kam: Sĩkũkũ mbingĩ ila syĩkawa nĩ kanĩsa syĩnthaa syĩ sya kũtanĩa maũlĩlĩkanyo ma kanĩsa kana kũnengana kyeo kanĩsanĩ o kana maũndĩ a ngĩ manene makonanĩtye kanĩsa.
eng: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

kam: Mathau ma ithembo ya Kerala mendeesya muno uyiloela, vethwaa na nzou syiatianie mbanakavye, wini wa ithembo na mathau angi.
eng: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

kam: Wonany'o wa nthi yonthe (wisikie ta World Exposition, kana kwa laisi Expo) ni iseso inene ya ati na saenzi ya nthi yonthe.
eng: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

kam: nthĩ ĩla syĩna ũsolĩ na masomo ma kwonany'a mĩkalĩle namaũndũ mavĩtũkũ ĩtũmĩaa ĩwanza sya nthĩ.
eng: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

kam: International Horticultural Expoitions ni syathe ila syonanasya malaa, miunda ya kusomea ulu wa miti na syindu ingi ila syiilenie na miti.
eng: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

kam: O na ketha andu maasyaa no sitiwe kila mwaka (ketha syi nthi syi kivathukany'o) indi mekoni ni kuvathukanyo.
eng: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

kam: Maũndũ aa mekala vandũ va myei ĩtatũ na thanthatũ, namethiawa kũndũ kwĩna mwanya utanyiva heka 50.
eng: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

kam: Ve mithemba mingi kivathukany'o ya sinema ila itumiitwe myaka mingi mithelu. Ta ya milimita 35 (36 kwa milimita 24 nengativu) niyo itumiawa muno.
eng: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

kam: Nĩ laisi kũkwata ĩngĩ kwa vaatĩ wamĩna ĩla wĩ nayo, na yĩthaa na kwolĩtĩ ĩtĩanĩe vanini na DSLR ĩla yĩ vo kwa saa ii.
eng: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

kam: Kamela imwe sya sinema ya fomati ya kati kati itumiaa fomati ya sendimita 6 kwa 6, ianene nda na negative ya milimita 56 kwa 56.
eng: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

kam: Ino inenganae visa ntheu kundu kuna kwa ila ya nekativu ya milimita 35 ila ni 3136 sikwea kwa 864.
eng: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

kam: Nyamu sya kitheka nisyo kati wa syindu imwe syivinya kwa mukuni wa visa, na syendaa vaati nzeo, umiisyo, utuika na miio miseo.
eng: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

kam: Visa sya nyamu sya kitheka nivuthiiw'e, indi ta visa ila ingi, visa yithiawa yi lato ndeto ngili.
eng: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

kam: Ukuni wa visa wa nyamu sya kithekani kwendaa lenzi ndaasa, ona vala syindũ sya ikundi sya tũsũni kana tusamũ tũnini twendaa lenzi ingi.
eng: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

kam: Nyamu mbingi sya kuka syiyonekanaa muno na andu ni mavatitwe kuikuna visa sya kusevya mbesa nasyo.
eng: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

kam: Nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ nosyĩthe syĩna w'ĩa kana syĩna ũngendu. Mawĩ'thyũlũlũko nomethe me mathĩthũ, mavyũ kana memathũkũ.
eng: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

kam: Kwi ithyomo mbee wa 5,000 iulu wa nthi ve ithyomo mbee wa 20 iuneenwa ni andu mililion 50 kana ainge mbee wa asu.
eng: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

kam: Ndeto siandikitwe maita maingi syithiawa syi mituki kuelewa mbee wa ndeto sya kuneena, o ingi. Uu maita maingi niw'o uw'o wa masanduku ma valua, ala kaingi methiawa vinya kumatamuka nesa.
eng: Written words are often easier to understand than spoken words, also. This is especially true of addresses, which are often difficult to pronounce intelligibly.

kam: Nthi syonthe vyu mbingi ni syisi Kisungu nesa, na o na kwa mbingaingi no wikwaty'e umanyi muthime - muno muno anduni ma myaka nini.
eng: Many entire nations are completely fluent in English, and in even more you can expect a limited knowledge - especially among younger people.

kam: Sũanĩa, ethĩwa nĩũkwenda, mũ Mancu, mũ Bostoni, mũ Jamaica na mũ Sydneysider mailye mesanĩ kĩthyũlũlũ maiya ky'aũya kya ma'ĩyoo Toronto.
eng: Imagine, if you will, a Mancunian, Bostonian, Jamaican and Sydneysider sitting around a table having dinner at a restaurant in Toronto.

kam: maendee kwilegal mo mbene na ngewa kuma misyi minene ya kwoo, maitavanya na luka ya kwoo na argoti ya uvonge.
eng: They're regaling each other with stories from their hometowns, told in their distinct accents and local argot.

kam: Kuthooa liu ndukani nene vyu ni yo ithiawa nzia laisi vyu ya kuvuuna. Vatee my'anya ya kũua, ũnyuvi o na vamwe na uu withiawa usiiwe ni liu ula wi mũue.
eng: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food.

kam: Suvamaketi nisyiendee ukwata mbau nundu wa kuua liu woo. O na ingi nisyithwaa na maasini ya kuvyuvya liu.
eng: Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food.

kam: Nthini wa nthi imwe kana nduka nene syi kivathukany'o nivethiawa vainyiva mukaawa umwe wi nthini, muno muno utai ta wi vata muno na wa thooa munini.
eng: In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

kam: Umĩthya na ũikua mathangũ maku ma kũĩvwa kũkethĩwa na mbanga kana thĩna vamwe na namba ĩla mũũngamĩi waku ũtonya ũkwatĩkana nam'yo.
eng: Make and carry copies of your policy and your insurer's contact details with you.

kam: Mailite kwonia ula ukũivia e-mail na namba ya simu ni kenda matawe/ metikilwe na menyielesye.
eng: They need to show the insurer's e-mail address and international phone numbers for advice/authorizations and making claims.

kam: Ithiwa na kopi ingi miioni yaku na mutandaoni (itumie kwa isanduku yaku ya valua, kana yiyitwe nthini wa "matu").
eng: Have another copy in your luggage and online (e-mail to yourself with attachment, or stored in the "cloud").

kam: ketha kũtembea na kompyũta nĩnĩ sya kwoko, kũĩya mũvywano nthĩnĩ wa mwanyanĩ wa yo wakũĩya syĩndũ (nĩlĩkwatĩkana vate mũtandao).
eng: If traveling with a laptop or tablet, store a copy in its memory or disc (accessible without the internet).

kam: O na ingi nengane mathangu ma wiw'ano na namba sya utumia ukuvikia kwi ala mwi kyaloni nao na andu ma musyi kana nduu ila ikwenda utethya.
eng: Also give policy/contact copies to traveling companions and relatives or friends back home willing to help.

kam: Ng'ondi ni nyamu sya kau indi ni syisiaa ila kwina thina.
eng: Moose (also known as elk) aren't inherently aggressive, but will defend themselves if they perceive a threat.

kam: Ĩla andũ matekwona ndaatai nene ta ite nthũku, nomatonye ũthi vakuvĩ namy'o na kwĩlikya mbanganĩ.
eng: When people don't see moose as potentially dangerous, they may approach too closely and put themselves at risk.

kam: kũnywa mbũkĩ wĩna kĩthĩmo. Mbũkĩ ĩthũa kĩla mũndũ kĩvathũkang'anyo, na wĩsĩ kĩthĩmo chakũ nĩ kĩtũmĩ kĩnene.
eng: Drink alcoholic drinks with moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, and knowing your limit is very important.

kam: Mundu anywa uki muno no utonya kwanangika mbio, akatwika kilalinda kana akakwa.Mbanga ii niyongelekaa ila msundu anya uki ula utemvitukithye kunyuwa.
eng: Possible long term health events from excessive drinking can include liver damage and even blindness and death. The potential danger is increased when consuming illegally produced alcohol.

kam: Mbuki ila ngune muungu nitonya kwithiwa syina syindu syi muisyo ta methanoo, ila itumaa metho maa kana kikwu ona yi nini.
eng: Illegal spirits can contain various dangerous impurities including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small doses.

kam: Miwani no yithwe na thoowa munini nthi sya nza munomuno nthi syi ukwati munini kula ivalua syievawa thowa munini.
eng: Eyeglasses can be cheaper in a foreign country, especially in low-income countries where labour costs are lower.

kam: Suania kwusiiw'a metho musyi, muno muno ethiwa aivi ma ngalama nimamiongelete vo, na kuete vala uandikiwe ndawa vaseuviw'e kundu kungi.
